Primary order stays `prefer`: if one family keeps failing first for a capability, narrow its `prefer` rather than reorder primaries globally. **Not changed.** `attemptProviderCapacityFallback` (the legacy dispatch path and workflow operations that declare `policy.fallbackExecutors`) is a second walker that leases by family key without the CLI and does not use the walk; the write gate recomputes without `independentOf` and `preferIndependentOf`, so a spread-chosen primary can differ from the recompute; per-capability tier ceilings and spend tracking are not built. Component boundary: no change (`bind()` decides candidates, the lease decides accounts).
  - Phần chọn ghế của rule này bị D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice) thay một phần, 2026-10-20: authority đích là [seat-binding.md](../../../seat-binding/spec.md); code đổi cùng plan của nó. Chữ rule ở trên không sửa tại chỗ.
- **(herdr panes open through terminal-control, 2026-10-18; the round itself moved to the run supervisor, same day).** A herdr seat no longer has a round loop in the controller: the controller prepares the attempt (brief, home, trust seed, `allocate(key = attempt id, groupKey)`), writes a `terminal`-mode envelope and hands it to the run supervisor, which opens, briefs, watches and releases the pane through `fgos-terminal-control` (`docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md` section 5.3, `docs/platform/terminal-control/spec.md`). The group key is the dispatch batch key, else the unit run id, so every attempt of one batch lands in one tab; `FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE` is an `attach` into that group. A failed or stopped attempt's pane is kept until a person closes it (a positive `terminal.retainFailedPaneMs` only makes doctor report the pane with its pane id once that time has passed; nothing closes it) and a finished one is closed once by `release-slot`; `terminal.layout.*` and `terminal.allocationGraceMs` reach the route from the project (then global) config, and doctor's `terminal-control` and `terminal-allocations` checks show what an attempt would use. Starting a herdr server for a confined session stays in `worker-session-boot.mjs` (a server lifecycle, not a pane operation).
- **(a private home belongs to its attempt, 2026-10-18; ends the confinement orphan reaper).** Only adopt's finalize-home step removes the private home of an attempt, while the attempt lock is free and its process domain is empty; the sweep (`sweepAttempts`) is adopt alone. The pane, binder and expiry rules, `bind`/`markLaunched`/`retain`, the post-probe sweep and the herdr-launch-command write are removed; a herdr-spawn launch needs an attempt id. Why: the old rules judged a home by a pid, a pane or an age, which could take the home of a worker still running (S2); one owner removes that class of fault. Left open: a dispatch outside the assignment door that dies leaves its home (named by `fgos doctor`, removed only by an explicit `doctor --fix`, never swept), and `fgos run` no longer has a startup rule for homes written with a pane binding by an older release.
- **(a Unit carries its own verify and skills, verify runs bounded, and a reviewed run at rigor high or critical needs a family per seat, 2026-10-18; owner decisions 2026-10-18; the rigor part supersedes decision 0055 for `reviewed` only).**
  - **`verify` stays on the Unit.** `validateUnit` keeps `verify` (a non-empty shell command) and `skills` (a non-empty list of skill names, trimmed, de-duplicated) through validation, the units-file loader, the workflow template and the round; a registered workflow template may set both too.
  - **Where the verify command comes from.** `verifyCommandOf` (`patterns/reviewed.mjs`) reads the Unit's own `verify`, else its capability's `verify`, and nothing else; the `code-change` preset pins none (it used to name `npm test`, which no runner ever executed, so a reviewed run recorded a verify pass that checked nothing), and `params.verify` no longer counts. A reviewed run with no verify command still passes on its checkers but its result carries `verify: { ran: false, reason }`; a solo or panel run, which has no verify step, says nothing.
  - **One bounded runner.** The verify step runs through `runCommand` (`src/runner/goal-check.mjs`, the same runner `return` and `approve` use) in the Unit's worktree, for at most `runner.timeoutMs` (the existing key and default; no new key, so nothing new for setup or doctor to register). A non-zero exit, a command that could not start and one that ran past the limit are each a failed verify that becomes findings naming the status (`exited N`, `timed out after Nms`, `could not run`) and the last twenty lines of output; none of them hangs the run.
  - **One-liner flags.** `fgos run "<prompt>" --input <a>,<b> --verify "<cmd>"` set the Unit's `inputs` and `verify`; both are refused beside `--unit` or `--resume`, and an empty value is refused before any unit run exists.
  - **Skills reach `bind()`.** `bind()` skips an executor whose `supports.skills` (new optional key in the executor's `supports` block, a non-empty array of names) does not list every skill the Unit names; none left refuses with reason `skills-unavailable` naming the missing skills, and the session lead never takes over such a Unit inline. Only roles that do the Unit's work are asked for skills: checker, panel and debate roles (`reviewer`, `red-team`, `tester`, `panelist*`, `synthesizer`, `thesis`, `antithesis`, `judge`) are chosen on independence alone. An executor that declares no `supports.skills` provides none. `fgos doctor` check `executor-skills-installed` fails when a declared skill has no `SKILL.md` in its runtime's skill directory of the main checkout (by each invocation's CLI: `claude` reads `.claude/skills/<name>`, `codex` `.agents/skills/<name>`, `omp` `.omp/skills/<name>`, `pi` `.pi/skills/<name>`, `grok` `.grok/skills/<name>`, and an executor passes only when every invocation's directory has the skill; `ak:cook` is the directory `ak-cook`); `worktreeSetup.commands` copies the untracked `ak-*` skill directories from the main checkout into each new worktree, so a worker sees them. `fgos worktree create` records what its provisioning placed (`provisionWorktree` in `src/runner/worktree.mjs`: every new untracked or ignored path, with a content digest for a file and the target for a symlink, and the `node_modules` it installed declared regenerable) in `<stateRoot>/worktree-provisioning/<sha256 of the checkout's real path>.json`, bound to the checkout directory's device and inode. `fgos worktree remove` moves exactly those bytes into a sibling directory before the Git port's clean check (`setProvisionedAside`): a copy only while it still matches its digest, and a recorded directory only once it is empty. It moves them back when the port refuses and deletes them, with the record, once the port has removed the checkout. A worker-edited copy or any byte the record does not name stays in place, and the port refuses on it. The brief for an `ak:cook` worker is `core/skills/_shared/ak-cook-worker-contract.md`.
  - **`docs:write`** is a curated capability slot (`DEFAULT_CAPABILITY_SLOTS`, description-only, `serves: { outputKind: change, domain: docs, mutates: true }`) next to `code:implement`, so `fgos setup` declares the capability the one-liner and `fgos-run` name for documentation work.
  - **Rigor high or critical: every seat of a `reviewed` run on its own family.** When the Unit's rigor, or its capability's rigor floor (the stronger of the two, as `bind()` computes it), is `high` or `critical`, each checker is `independentOf` the producer and of every other checker (`requiresDistinctFamilies`), a fallback walk after a provider limit re-reads that list so the replacement keeps the property, and a pool without enough families refuses the seat that cannot be placed with the existing reason `independence`. Standard and low keep the old rule (checker differs from the producer only). Decision 0055's soft spread is unchanged for `panel`: seat count there is still not capped by family count (owner, 2026-10-11).
  - **`debate`: two sides soft, the judge hard.** `runDebate` (`patterns/debate.mjs`) dispatches `thesis` and `antithesis` read-only with `preferIndependentOf` each other (a shared family is reported, not refused), optionally a second round where each side gets only the other's round-1 result in `inputs`, then `judge` with `independentOf: [thesis, antithesis]` and every result as `inputs`. The judge's family differing from both sides is the one hard independence rule of the pattern; an unseatable judge is bind()'s named `independence` refusal (`policy-refusal` outcome), never a same-family ruling. The three roles are listed once, in `CHECKER_ROLES` of `bind.mjs`, so they never run inline or in-process and are not asked for the Unit's skills. `fgos doctor`'s pool-independence check drives the same pattern code, so a pool with too few families fails it before a run. `unit-summary` gives the sides seat kind `producer` and the judge `judge`.

- **RUL101 (the per-worktree dispatch lock is a kernel lock held through holder-lock; a dead holder releases at once, 2026-10-16).** The lock a dispatch takes on its working directory (`dispatch-cwd`, rank 30, kind `lease`, scope still `fgosDir`) is a kernel lock on an open file description, acquired through the holder-lock facade (`src/holder-lock/`, authority `docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md`), with the cwd keyed by `dev:ino` after `realpath`. The lock file is `<fgosDir>/locks/dispatch-cwd--<dev>-<ino>.lock`, so one directory reached through a symlink is one lock; a cwd that does not exist fails as `worker-spawn-fail` before any lock. There is no holder record, no `ttlMs`, no heartbeat renewal and no reclaim by a contender: the kernel releases the lock when every process holding the description has died, so a holder killed without releasing, with or without a reused pid, blocks nobody; a live holder that is wedged keeps it until it exits. `sharedCwd` and `forceSharedCwd` still take no lock. A second dispatch on a held cwd fails `dispatch-in-flight` naming the holder pid. The resume guard of `fgos run --resume` and the reconcile planner read the kernel's holder list (`lockHolders`, which takes no lock) and fall back to `probe(dispatch-cwd)` (one non-blocking shared try) only where holders cannot be listed, since a shared try could make a concurrent one-try acquire see `held`; they refuse on a holder, neither judges a holder alive or dead, and a lock that cannot be read is never read as free. The legacy `.fgos/dispatch--<cwd>.lock` path is fenced by a tombstone at cutover for every worktree and claim, in both the `path.resolve` and the `realpath` form; `fgos dispatch reconcile clear-cwd-lock` only reports held or free and never clears a cwd lock. The reconcile planner's own local lock (`reconcile`, rank 80) is a kernel mutex at `<fgosDir>/locks/reconcile.lock` under the same port. Order inside one `LockScope` is enforced at acquire: a lock taken at a rank not above every rank the scope already holds throws `lock-order-violation` at once, with no trace-then-warn release.
- **RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool; one family has one executor; llmAccounts is read for checking only, 2026-10-17).** A cell of `runner.modelPolicies.<family>.<tier>` is a model, a model served by a named pool (`model@pool`), or a non-empty ordered list of those. The pool is the service provider that bills the call. A cell entry is split at its last `@`, so a model id that itself contains `@` names its pool explicitly (`claude-opus-4@20250514@vertex`); an entry without `@` is served by the pool named after the family. There is no default-pool key. A run uses the first entry served by the family's own pool (`resolveTierModel`); `resolveTierCandidates` returns every entry for `fgos dispatch explain` and doctor. An entry served by another pool is accepted and never run until the lease routes pools; a cell with no entry for the family's pool counts as a missing tier, which still falls back to the executor's own `model` or the CLI default. The project config accepts every form. The global `~/.fgos/config.json` is read by every fgOS release on the machine, and an older release fails on a list and passes `model@pool` to the CLI as a model id, so a list or `@` cell there is dropped with a warning naming the cell (once per process), and doctor `global-model-policies-portable` fails on it.
  Each agent family (`providerModel`) is served by exactly one executor; its transports (headless cli, herdr pane, sandboxed or not) are invocations of that executor, and `bind()` picks the pane invocation inside herdr and a cli one outside, so a capability gets the same family and model in both places. Doctor `executor-family-unique` fails on a family with two agent executors.
  `runner.llmAccounts.<pool>.<account>` is the machine's account inventory, global-only: `credentialStore: { <cli>: <login directory> }` (`~`, `${HOME}` and `$HOME` expand), plus optional `label` and `disabled`. A pool name is the family name for the family's own vendor and the provider's name otherwise (`openrouter`); it may not contain `@` nor be another spelling of a configured family (`codex`, `openai-codex`, `glm`, `agy`). `readLlmAccounts` reports problems instead of throwing; `compareWithLegacyInventory` sets it against `runner.providers.<provider>.accounts` by the state key the lease uses (`openai` is `openai-codex` there). The lease, account pins and credential provisioning still read `runner.providers` only. Doctor: `llm-accounts-shape` fails on any reader problem, `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` warns on accounts or login directories that differ once `llmAccounts` is declared, `model-policy-pools` warns on a cell naming a pool `llmAccounts` does not declare.
  `fgos dispatch explain --for <capability> [--rigor <r>]` binds the capability through `bind()` and reports the family and the `prefer` entry that chose it, the tier, its source (rigor, override) and its ceiling (RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat; a capability's own rigor raises its own ceiling)), the whole cell with each entry marked `used`, `fallback-same-pool` or `pending-pool-routing`, the executor and invocation, and the pool's accounts in both inventories. It leases, spawns and writes nothing.
- **RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat; a capability's own rigor raises its own ceiling, 2026-10-17).** `runner.maxTier`, when set, is the highest tier a seat runs at, whatever asked for the tier: the unit's rigor, the capability's rigor floor, or an override (`--override '{"tier":...}'`). A capability that declares its own `rigor` in `runner.capabilities` raises the ceiling for its own seats to `rigorToTier[rigor]` when that tier is higher. The ceiling of a seat is therefore the higher of `runner.maxTier` and the tier of its capability's declared rigor (`resolveTierCeiling` in `bind.mjs`); a unit's rigor and an override stay under it, so only the config decides which capabilities may run above the cap, and a frontier override on a capability declaring `high` stops at `flagship`. Without `runner.maxTier` there is no ceiling. A capability cannot be held below the global cap this way. The binding records the ceiling on `provenance.tier.ceiling` as `{ value, source }`, `source` being `global` or `capability-rigor(<capability>, <rigor>)`; a clamped tier's source reads `clamped:maxTier(<tier>, <ceiling source>)`. `fgos dispatch explain` shows the ceiling, and doctor `capability-rigor-ceiling` lists the capabilities lifted above `runner.maxTier` with the tier and model they run at; it never fails. The assignment policy (`resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy`) raises the tier `bind()` hands it and applies no ceiling, so when `bind()` clamped, the policy's recorded tier can read higher than the tier that ran; the model is always the one `bind()` chose.
textCatalog.86688e71bf8e6321a26a222e59c5263a5e412266:
- **RUL1 (sự thật duy nhất là nhật ký sự kiện append-only, bản chiếu chỉ là dẫn xuất).** Trong vòng dispatch, runner là người ghi duy nhất qua một cửa; worker không bao giờ tự ghi trạng thái (per phase-2-routing / feed7428).
- **RUL2 (mọi mutation đi qua đúng một cửa ghi).** Kết quả worker là ĐỀ XUẤT mức bền: commit trên nhánh `fgw/` (do runner tạo từ file worker để lại, không phải worker tự commit — 0052), phải qua người duyệt mới thành `done`; không bao giờ tự merge (auto-merge là backlog STR9).
- **RUL3 (thứ tự ghi bất biến: sự kiện vào nhật ký trước, bản chiếu cập nhật sau).** Runner tự chạy proof của việc làm goal-check — lời trợ lý không bao giờ là bằng chứng.
- **RUL4 (giao việc theo mẻ, giới hạn hai tầng, quyền-sở-hữu-gốc giữ nguyên trong lượt chạy).** Một lượt chạy giao TỐI ĐA N việc cùng lúc, giới hạn qua cấu hình hai tầng — số gốc đồng thời × số con đồng thời mỗi gốc (Data Dictionary #6); mọi con của MỘT gốc luôn về tay cùng một chủ trong suốt một lượt chạy (Data Dictionary #7, xem RUL26 (quyền-sở-hữu-gốc — mọi con của một gốc về tay cùng một chủ trong một lượt chạy)); dispatch nạp lại mẻ tới khi không còn việc đang chạy VÀ không còn việc sẵn-sàng. Chống-lặp qua vận hành thật (A1) là điều kiện đã chứng minh TRƯỚC khi song song được dựng — không còn là một ngưỡng-tên treo chờ (per fan-out-parallel / 2e92b7a5).
- **RUL5 (ghi có kỳ vọng: trạng thái thực khác kỳ vọng thì từ chối, không ghi đè mù).** Model chọn theo tier của việc qua bảng cấu hình; tập tier reconcile một nguồn tại đây.
- **RUL6 (consumer rẽ nhánh theo mã thoát phạm trù, không bao giờ theo thông điệp).** Chống đỡ bằng CHỈ DẪN + nhánh-vứt-được, KHÔNG phải sandbox OS/container. Worker headless chạy dưới tập quyền TỐI THIỂU khai tường minh trong `.fgos/config.json`'s `runner.executor.args`: `--permission-mode acceptEdits` (tự nhận sửa file), **không** cấp quyền git — worker chỉ sửa file, runner commit thay (quyết định 0052; trước đó là `--allowedTools "Bash(git add:*),Bash(git commit:*)"`); `--dangerously-skip-permissions` bị BÁC có chủ đích (worker chỉ cần sửa-file + commit trong worktree, prompt đã cấm merge/push/tự gọi fgos, và goal-check không tin lời trợ lý — RUL13 (vòng dự đoán-thực tế, học từ cả thành công lẫn thất bại) — nên quyền rộng hơn là rủi ro không cần) (per worker-execution / 22699c61, 04a6cd05). Root cause spike-proven (2 biến thể, claude CLI thật): thiếu allowlist này, headless `claude -p` sửa file được nhưng `git commit` treo vô thời hạn chờ duyệt tương tác → nhánh đề xuất luôn rỗng, dispatch luôn đỗ. Bất biến phải giữ: work item (nhất là trường proof — được chạy như lệnh shell) do chính người dùng tạo; không bao giờ nạp việc từ nguồn ngoài khi chưa có vòng kiểm (security panel, ghi trong hợp đồng handoff).
- **RUL7 (schema item mang đủ chất liệu trả lời sáu câu hỏi harness).** Lớp lỗi lạ → dừng, không bao giờ mặc định thử-lại (fail-safe).
- **RUL8 (deps phải trỏ id tồn tại, cấm tự trỏ).** Bước gặt-lại làm chạy-lại-sau-crash an toàn tự thân: không việc nào vô hình, không commit đôi, không worktree rò (reliability panel — 3 blocker vá trước khi code).
- **RUL9 (thực thi khi dev).** Mọi kiểm chứng chạy trong Claude Code bằng subscription: suite dùng executor giả (0 token), worker thật qua claude CLI login. API key chỉ hợp lệ khi tính năng đang test là executor-cắm-ngoài, và là key của môi trường người dùng (per 774b73ef).
- **RUL10 (diễn tập không chạm log thật).** Nhật ký sự kiện append-only bất biến → một event diễn tập lọt vào là rác vĩnh viễn: canary/drill LUÔN chạy trên repo mồi dùng-xong-vứt; chỉ dogfood việc-thật mới ghi log thật — và đó là lịch sử vận hành chủ đích (per f3a16887).
- **RUL11 (thang kiểm chứng).** T0 suite executor-giả mọi commit · T1 dogfood việc thật hằng ngày · T1c canary khai-môi-trường (worker tự báo pwd/git-root/doctrine nó thấy, verify assert từng dòng) định kỳ và sau mỗi đổi harness · T2 máy-trắng (HOME giả + credential tối thiểu) trước release (per f3a16887). Bất biến nền: mỗi agent khởi đầu tại project-root CỦA NÓ — thợ ở xưởng, worker ở git-root của worktree nó đứng.
- **RUL12 (khoá liên-tiến-trình).** Mỗi kho chỉ một runner sống tại một thời điểm: đầu MỌI lần chạy (trước cả bước gặt-lại — gặt cũng ghi trạng thái), runner chiếm khoá độc quyền trong vùng trạng thái, ghi định danh tiến trình của mình. Kho đang có runner sống → lần chạy mới thoát «bận» bằng mã thoát riêng (không trùng mã nào hiện hành): không ghi trạng thái, không đụng worktree, không đụng khoá của người giữ. Khoá của runner đã chết (crash để lại, hoặc nội dung không chứng minh được chủ sống) → **dọn-rồi-nhường**: kiểm nội dung sát trước khi xoá (đổi rồi thì không đụng), xoá xong lượt đó vẫn lui ra «bận» — không lượt chạy nào vừa xoá khoá vừa tự chiếm trong cùng một lần, nên hai lượt cùng gặp khoá chết không thể cướp khoá mới của nhau; lượt kế tiếp chiếm khoá sạch (sau crash, phục hồi trọn trong hai lượt). Khoá luôn được nhả trên mọi đường thoát.
- **RUL13 (vòng dự đoán-thực tế, học từ cả thành công lẫn thất bại).** Mỗi lần dispatch, runner ghi bản ghi outcome ở CẢ hai đầu: nửa dự đoán lúc nhận việc, nửa thực tế ở MỌI kết cục cuối — thành đề xuất, bị đỗ, hay bị dừng — không bao giờ chỉ ghi khi thành công. Giá trị thực tế luôn lấy từ phép đo goal-check/kiểm nhánh của chính runner, không bao giờ từ báo cáo tự khai của trợ lý (per phase-3-compound-learning / 1a80b4d3; mở rộng nguyên tắc "không tin lời trợ lý" đã khóa ở RUL3 (thứ tự ghi bất biến: sự kiện vào nhật ký trước, bản chiếu cập nhật sau)). Bản ghi outcome đọc lại được qua lệnh đọc-thuần `fgos check` của tầng Work-State — runner không có verb ghi riêng cho việc này.
- **RUL14 (quét nghiên-cứu chạy trước dispatch, bất kể mode).** Mỗi lượt chạy, ngay sau gặt-lại và trước khi tìm việc thi công, runner GIAO TOÀN BỘ item đang ở stage `discovery` + `status: todo` cho một worker thật, rồi áp đúng phán quyết mà chính worker đó phát ra — không đọc/không rẽ nhánh theo field `mode` của item (per stage-clarify / 9a19eea5, xem RUL17 (quét chia-việc chạy ngay sau quét nghiên-cứu, trước dispatch, bất kể mode)-RUL19 (`return` mirror trung thực contract `awaiting-approval` của runner, không tin lời) (work-state)). Runner KHÔNG BAO GIỜ tự phán thay: worker không để lại commit nào, hoặc output không mang phán quyết đọc được, thì item đứng nguyên tại chỗ chờ lượt sau — không bao giờ bị đẩy tiếp bừa. Never chạm item `awaiting-human`, và cũng không chạm item đã có người/phiên cầm (`doing`) — cùng luật loại-trừ RUL6 (consumer rẽ nhánh theo mã thoát phạm trù, không bao giờ theo thông điệp) (work-state)/RUL15 (role trên mọi ngã-ngũ tự động của runner) (work-state) áp cho cả bước quét này. Stage `exploring` nằm NGOÀI mọi quét của vòng tự hành: nó là pha cần người, để dành cho một phiên sống. Đây là lưới đỡ: phiên submit sống chết giữa chừng không để lại việc kẹt vô hình. `discovery` là tên stage riêng của `coding`, không domain nào khác khai — nên phép khớp trực tiếp ở đây không bao giờ bắt nhầm item của một domain khác (xem spec Work-State "Mô hình domain").
- **RUL15 (role trên mọi ngã-ngũ tự động của runner).** Mọi ngã-ngũ mà runner TỰ ghi trong vòng dispatch (quét nghiên-cứu cho qua, quét chia-việc cho qua, nhận việc, đề xuất, đỗ) mang `role` = `runner`; ngã-ngũ do phiên sống gọi tay context-discovery/phán chia-việc mang `role` = `session`; ngã-ngũ do người gọi qua lệnh CLI mang `role` = `human` — ba giá trị phủ hết mọi đường ngã-ngũ hiện có, không đường nào bị bỏ sót (per phase-3-compound-learning S3-closeout / 96a65365; xem spec Work-State "Bản ghi settlement"). Từ vựng `role` nay có thêm giá trị thứ tư, `system` — cạnh do máy sinh ra như hệ quả của một verb, không do ai quyết định — dùng trên cạnh park nội bộ (per str46-io-contract, xem RUL29 (cổng chống-lặp reset theo can thiệp người cuối cùng của chính việc)); một cạnh park không phải một ngã-ngũ nên không tính vào ba giá trị trên.
- **RUL16 (điểm entropy luôn giải thích được + luôn kèm xu hướng).** Điểm entropy trên `metrics entropy` không bao giờ là một con số đơn độc — luôn kèm các thành phần đã cộng nên nó, và luôn so với snapshot gần nhất (lần đầu là baseline). Seal-digest chỉ im lặng một mệnh đề khi kênh đó thật sự không có gì để nói (số đếm hiện tại VÀ chênh lệch đều bằng 0) — một kênh có dữ liệu nhưng không đổi ...
- **RUL17 (quét chia-việc chạy ngay sau quét nghiên-cứu, trước dispatch, bất kể mode).** Mỗi lượt chạy, ngay sau quét nghiên-cứu và trước khi tìm việc thi công, runner đọc lại view tươi rồi quét TOÀN BỘ item ở stage thỏa bước Chia-việc của domain của chính nó (`planning` cho `coding`) — CỘNG THÊM item còn nằm ở tên stage di sản `decompose`, một alias chỉ-để-rút-cạn không item mới nào còn được tạo ở đó — với `status: todo`, rồi chạy phán chia-việc; không đọc/không rẽ nhánh theo field `mode` của item. Bước quét này KHÔNG gọi model: nó chỉ cho đi thẳng một item mà bản kế hoạch đã ghi tự khai là một-mảnh, mọi trường hợp khác nó không làm gì cả và chờ một phiên sống phán tay — sinh con là hành động ghi thật, không bao giờ được đoán. Never chạm item `awaiting-human` — cùng luật loại-trừ RUL6 (consumer rẽ nhánh theo mã thoát phạm trù, không bao giờ theo thông điệp) (work-state)/RUL15 (role trên mọi ngã-ngũ tự động của runner) (work-state) áp cho bước quét này. Đọc view tươi sau quét nghiên-cứu nghĩa là một item vừa rời `discovery` trong CÙNG lượt chạy vẫn được quét chia-việc ngay, không đợi lượt sau (per stage-decompose / 43f257ae, xem spec Work-State "Giai đoạn Chia-việc").
- **RUL18 (gặt-lại claim-role-aware — không giẫm người/phiên cầm qua cửa pull).** Bước gặt-lại lúc khởi động CHỈ gặt claim mà chính runner đã tạo và crash giữa chừng; một item `doing` mang `claimRole` `human`/`session` (đến từ `fgos take` — spec Work-State "Cửa pull giao–nhận việc") không bao giờ bị reclaim, dù nó không mang commit/proof nào — người/phiên cầm việc vô thời hạn cho tới khi chính họ `fgos return`. Đây là một THU HẸP thuần túy của tập item vốn đã bị reap — không mở rộng, không giảm an toàn của gặt-lại cho claim của chính runner (per stage-decompose, chốt tại validating sau 1 BLOCKER / 43f257ae, 6f2cbc47, a30a3d3c).
- **RUL19 (`return` mirror trung thực contract `awaiting-approval` của runner, không tin lời).** Cửa pull `return` chỉ chuyển `doing → awaiting-approval` sau khi TỰ đo — không tin báo cáo của người gọi — cả ba: working tree host repo sạch, HEAD tiến so `headAtTake` ghi lúc `take`, và verify thật của item chạy xanh qua CÙNG hàm goal-check runner dùng (`runGoalCheck`, `src/runner/goal-check.mjs`) — mở rộng nguyên tắc "không tin lời trợ lý" đã khóa ở RUL3 (thứ tự ghi bất biến: sự kiện vào nhật ký trước, bản chiếu cập nhật sau)/RUL13 (vòng dự đoán-thực tế, học từ cả thành công lẫn thất bại) sang tác nhân cửa pull. Verify đỏ đi đúng đường `blocked` + friction lớp `verification`, y hệt đường đỗ chấm-trượt của chính runner; không sinh settlement ở `return` (settlement thuộc cạnh `→done`, per stage-decompose — xem spec Work-State) (per stage-decompose / 43f257ae, 6f2cbc47, a30a3d3c).
- **RUL60 (`return` mang thêm khuyến nghị frozen-judge — advisory, không bao giờ chặn, per STR63).** Ngay khi `check.passed` (cả hai nhánh nguồn: branch-source qua `branchHeadAtTake→branchHead`, main-source qua `headAtTake→head`), `return` tính `changedFilesSince(cwd, from, to)` (`git diff --name-only`, KHÔNG dùng `changedFiles` của `merge.mjs` — hàm đó cố định trả `[]` cho item không phải nguồn runner, tức luôn rỗng với chính item cửa pull mà `return` phục vụ) rồi chấm qua `frozenJudgeHits(changedFiles, item.footprint)` (`src/runner/frozen-judge.mjs`, domain layer thuần — cổng mẫu `FROZEN_JUDGE_PATTERNS` bê nguyên từ frozen-judge của bee, khớp exact-path với `footprint` đã khai, không hỗ trợ prefix-thư-mục/glob, đúng quy ước `footprintOverlap` sẵn có). Kết quả gắn vào field `frozenJudgeHits` của JSON trả về — KHÔNG BAO GIỜ đổi `passed`/đường đi `blocked`, thuần advisory (per - str63-frozen-judge-fgos, xem forgent workshop `docs/history/str63-frozen-judge-fgos/CONTEXT.md`).
- **RUL20 (cổng duyệt là cửa MỘT DUY NHẤT cho mọi đề xuất, bất kể nguồn).** `review`/`approve`/`reject` hành động trên CẢ hai nguồn đề xuất — runner (nhánh `fgw/<id>`) và pull-door (dải `headAtTake→headAtReturn`) — qua cùng một luật, không hai bộ quy tắc song song; đề xuất di sản (thiếu cả nhánh lẫn cặp head) degrade trung thực (một cảnh báo, không throw) thay vì bị từ chối hoàn toàn (per pr-lifecycle / 1359ab5e).
- **RUL21 (merge sạch → done tự động; gãy → hủy sạch merge dở + blocked có lý do).** `approve` trên nguồn runner không bao giờ để main ở trạng thái merge dở trên bất kỳ đường thoát nào: conflict hoặc verify đỏ sau merge đều `git merge --abort` (main nguyên vẹn byte-for-byte, chứng minh bằng spike + test thật) rồi đậu item ở `blocked` mang lý do cụ thể (`merge-conflict`/`verify-fail-post-merge`) — KHÔNG tự rebase, KHÔNG halt cả vòng runner. `done` qua approve luôn mang role `human` (per pr-lifecycle / 1359ab5e — người chạy approve là ngã-ngũ, merge chỉ là hệ quả cơ học, per vision §8 "người ở cổng").
- **RUL22 (reject không bao giờ đảo lịch sử).** `reject` là một move FSM thuần `awaiting-approval→todo` mang `reason`; không bao giờ gọi một lệnh git nào, kể cả cho một đề xuất pull-door đã có code thật trên main — code đó ở lại như lịch sử, `reject` chỉ từ-chối coi-là-xong, không revert/rewrite (per pr-lifecycle / 1359ab5e).
- **RUL23 (phản hồi người threading vào prompt worker).** Prompt dựng cho worker (`buildPrompt`) mang thêm một mục `# Human feedback` TÙY CHỌN khi item mang câu trả lời làm-rõ mới nhất (fold từ cổng chờ-người, xem spec Work-State "Bản ghi cổng-người") và/hoặc lý do từ-chối/đỗ mới nhất (`item.reason`, xem spec Work-State Data Dictionary #18): câu trả lời in NGUYÊN VĂN dưới nhãn quyết-định-cuối-cùng-ràng-buộc, lý do mới nhất in NGUYÊN VĂN dưới nhãn ưu-tiên-sửa-trước-tiên. Vắng cả hai → mục này KHÔNG xuất hiện, prompt giữ nguyên byte-identical hình cũ (cộng thêm thuần, không phá vỡ hợp đồng 4 section pin sẵn có). Runner đọc lại view TƯƠI ngay trước khi spawn worker (item truyền vào dispatch có thể cũ hơn move gần nhất của chính lượt gặt-lại/quét) rồi truyền `feedback: {answer, reason}` xuống `spawnWorker`. Đây là cách một vòng reject hội tụ: dogfood-thật cho thấy không có mục này, worker vòng sau lặp lại đúng đề xuất vừa bị từ chối vì không thấy lý do (per worker-execution STR33 / 396d9d9e).
- **RUL24 (một-người-ghi vẫn giữ nguyên dưới song song, qua một cửa ghi tuần tự).** Dù nhiều việc thi công đồng thời trong một mẻ, MỌI thay đổi trạng thái (nhận việc, đề xuất, đỗ, nhập) đi qua ĐÚNG một cửa ghi tuần tự — một giao dịch ghi trọn vẹn rồi mới tới giao dịch kế tiếp, không bao giờ hai thay đổi chen lẫn nhau giữa chừng. Đây là hệ quả trực tiếp của RUL1 (sự thật duy nhất là nhật ký sự kiện append-only, bản chiếu chỉ là dẫn xuất) dưới điều kiện mới: song song ở việc THỰC THI (nhiều worker chạy đồng thời), không phải ở việc GHI (per fan-out-parallel).
- **RUL25 (cây chính chỉ nhận nguyên một tính năng đã xong, không mảnh dở — SUPERSEDE quyết định trước đó).** Một việc CON không bao giờ nhập thẳng vào cây chính — nó nhập vào nhánh của GỐC nó; chỉ đề xuất của chính GỐC (sau khi mọi con đã xong) mới nhập vào cây chính, đúng một lần cho cả tính năng. Điều này THAY quyết định trước đây ("mỗi việc một đề xuất, thẳng vào cây chính") trong bối cảnh một việc có con — quyết định cũ vẫn đúng nguyên vẹn cho một việc ĐỘC LẬP (không con), đi thẳng đường cũ không đổi (per fan-out-parallel / 2e92b7a5, supersede-in-context quyết định pr-lifecycle).
- **RUL26 (quyền-sở-hữu-gốc — mọi con của một gốc về tay cùng một chủ trong một lượt chạy).** Lúc con ĐẦU TIÊN của một gốc được nhận trong một lượt chạy, gốc đó gắn chủ; con tiếp theo của CÙNG gốc chỉ được nhận bởi ĐÚNG chủ đó — một chủ khác giành nhận bị từ chối (cùng khuôn kỳ-vọng-lệch của mọi cửa nhận việc khác), việc đó ở lại chờ mẻ sau. Chủ xả khi gốc xong. Bảo vệ nguyên tắc "mọi con của một gốc chung một không gian làm việc" (per fan-out-parallel).
- **RUL27 (nhập gốc→cây chính bắt CẢ xung đột văn bản LẪN trôi ngữ nghĩa im lặng).** Một GỐC từng có con, lúc nhập vào cây chính, được kiểm CẢ hai: nhập có xung đột văn bản không, VÀ sau khi nhập (chưa chốt) verify của chính gốc còn xanh không trên cây đã nhập — verify đỏ ở bước này là TRÔI ngữ nghĩa (nhập sạch nhưng kết hợp gãy), bị coi ngang xung đột văn bản: hủy sạch, cây chính không bao giờ giữ một nhập xanh-mà-gãy (per fan-out-parallel / f0c40acc). Vì đây là phép kiểm DUY NHẤT cho cả cây hậu duệ, verify của gốc phải đủ mạnh lúc soạn — verify mỏng bỏ lọt trôi ngữ nghĩa.
- **RUL28 (đồng bộ-lại sạch = cơ học không đếm; làm-lại tay = có đếm).** Một việc đỗ vì gãy nhập được đồng bộ-lại: nếu sau khi kéo đích mới nhất vào, nhập sạch VÀ verify xanh, việc trở lại sẵn sàng nộp lại theo đường cơ học (không qua "đang làm", không tính vào ngân sách chống-lặp của việc) — phân biệt với người CHỌN cầm việc qua cửa pull để tự làm-lại tay, đường đó QUA "đang làm" như bình thường và ĐƯỢC đếm (per fan-out-parallel).
- **RUL29 (cổng chống-lặp reset theo can thiệp người CUỐI CÙNG của chính việc, per-item, trigger-set đóng, executing-phase-only scoping).** Cổng chặn dispatch (khác `visitCount` lifetime metric ở RUL13 (vòng dự đoán-thực tế, học từ cả thành công lẫn thất bại) — xem Data Dictionary #4/#4b) đếm `visitsSinceLastHumanEvent`: số lần việc vào `doing` **ở stage executing của chính domain** KỂ TỪ sự kiện người cuối cùng của CHÍNH việc đó. Trước claim-lock (str83-fgos-slash-commands), `take`/`pick` chỉ mở frontier (executing-stage items), nên counting lifetime `todo→doing` moves tương đương counting chỉ dispatch attempts thực. Claim-lock cho phép `pick --id` cầm item ở các stage đầu vòng (`discovery`/`exploring`/`planning`, cộng tên di sản `decompose`) — một claim-release cycle ở đó (pick → phán chia-việc release `doing→todo` → pick lại ở executing) KHÔNG phải attempt dispatch và không được silent-ăn ngân sách của executing-phase attempts thực (per claim-lock §3a/§3c). Số liệu dẫn xuất chỉ từ `to:'doing'` moves mà item đã ở executing stage (mirror frontier.mjs's eligibility check). Trigger-set đóng — chỉ hai hình reset: việc rời `awaiting-human` bằng một câu trả lời của người (`answer`, role `human`), hoặc một move mang `reason` VỚI role `human` (reject/park do người quyết). Một lần resume trần (`blocked→todo` không `reason`), một lần người `take` việc (`blocked→doing`, role `human`, không `answer`/`reason`), và mọi move của chính runner (kể cả park mang `reason` của chính nó) đều KHÔNG reset — chỉ tính là một visit như mọi lần khác. Không có sự kiện người nào của việc → ngân sách bằng đúng lifetime `visitCount` executing-scoped (một vòng lỗi máy thuần vẫn chết ở trần 3, không đổi). `MAX_VISITS=3` và mọi call site của `visitCount` (outcome/metric đã ship) giữ nguyên — chỉ điểm CHẶN DISPATCH đổi công thức đếm (per human-rounds / 5a6900b2, per claim-lock §6 / code-review finding).
- **RUL30 (cửa người-hoàn-tất một đề xuất nguồn-nhánh bị đỗ — mở rộng take/return, không verb mới).** Một việc `blocked` mang nhánh đề xuất còn sống (`fgw/<id>`) — kể cả bị đỗ do chạm trần chống-lặp — có cửa công khai để người hoàn tất: `take` claim qua cạnh `blocked→doing` sẵn có, ghi `branchHeadAtTake` (HEAD của NHÁNH lúc take — discriminator DUY NHẤT của nguồn-nhánh, không dùng `classifySource` để phân biệt vì nó ưu-tiên-nhánh); người commit thêm lên nhánh; `return` kiểm `branchHeadAtTake` TRƯỚC mọi guard main-based (cây làm việc chính của người không bao giờ bị đọc/đụng), verify chạy trong một worktree TẠM, DETACHED tại đúng SHA của nhánh (không bao giờ checkout theo tên, không `reclaimOrphanedCheckout` — an toàn cả khi người đang đứng trên chính nhánh đó ở một worktree khác) → sạch + xanh → `awaiting-approval` mang `branchHeadAtReturn`; **TUYỆT ĐỐI không ghi `headAtReturn`** cho nguồn-nhánh (trộn hai marker cho `reviewDiff` một dải vô nghĩa). Không commit mới trên nhánh, hoặc verify đỏ trong worktree tạm → từ chối rõ lý do, việc giữ nguyên `doing`. Một đề xuất hoàn tất theo đường này đọc nguồn là `runner` như bình thường (nhánh `fgw/<id>` còn sống — không cần đổi `classifySource`/`merge.mjs`) và đi qua CÙNG cổng duyệt PR nội bộ (per human-rounds / 5a6900b2, xem spec Work-State "Cửa pull giao–nhận việc").
textCatalog.5726b14f8d6640b427325590516eae1a3f3d5288: - **RUL62 (`return --no-new-commits-ok` — đóng sổ việc đã xong THẬT từ trước lúc claim, không phải "tin lời").** Khi `branchAheadCount`/`aheadCount` <= 0 (chưa có commit mới kể từ `branchHeadAtTake`/`headAtTake`) NHƯNG cờ `--no-new-commits-ok` được truyền, `return` bỏ qua đúng MỘT bước — throw "chưa tiến" — rồi tiếp tục y hệt đường thường: verify thật vẫn chạy qua CÙNG `runGoalCheck`, xanh mới `awaiting-approval` (ghi `actual.aheadCount: 0`), đỏ vẫn `blocked` + friction lớp `verification` như thường (cờ không bao giờ tắt verify). Trước khi bỏ qua, một cổng riêng (`assertNoPriorBlockedOutcome`) từ chối cờ nếu `outcomes[id].actual.outcome` từng là `'blocked'` bất kỳ lúc nào trong lịch sử item (toàn item, không chỉ lượt claim hiện tại — `view.outcomes[id].actual` sống sót qua một lượt tái-claim vì tái-claim chỉ ghi `predicted`, không đụng `actual`) — chặn đúng lỗ hổng cờ có thể mở: tái claim một việc đã `blocked` thật, gọi cờ với không commit mới, hy vọng verify xanh vì lý do khác. Cờ chỉ đóng sổ việc CHƯA từng return, không bao giờ cứu một lượt thử lại đã thất bại thật. A seat that leases an account (an out-of-process agent that is not a tool) needs the cell; an in-process, inline or tool seat needs none and binds with `pool: null`. **Primary.** The first binding follows `prefer` order exactly as before, with the soft family spread of the panel seats unchanged, so council seats keep leading with different families. **After a failure** the walk takes, in order: the failed family's remaining cell entries, then the families `runner.tierFallback.` lists, limited to the families `prefer` names (a list narrows and never widens); with no list for the tier, the rest of the `prefer` order after the failed candidate. A walk never leaves its tier. The soft spread stays active in a walk and ranks the passing candidates, ties falling to walk order; without a spread request the walk takes the first untried candidate. **`runner.tierFallback`** is `{ : [family, ...] }` with the tiers of `modelPolicies`, each a non-empty list of distinct family names (the `modelPolicies` key, so GLM is `z-ai`); `validateTierFallbackShape` refuses anything else at load naming the key path, `tierFallbackOf` reads it, and doctor `tier-fallback` warns on a listed family with no cell at that tier or no agent executor. The code enforces the tier boundary and the narrowing only; the owner's groups are configuration: doer tiers (nano, standard, advanced) fall back across gemini, deepseek, z-ai, then claude, openai; flagship and frontier across claude, openai, gemini and xai. An older release ignores the unknown runner key, so the lists go in the project config. **Walk state** is the seat's earlier bindings (`tried`, identity = executor, invocation, pool and model), rebuilt from the attempts in `unit.json` by `triedBindingsOf`; `excludePools` replaces `excludeFamilies`: a dead login excludes that pool, not the family's other pools (RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine per pool) supersedes the walk of 0058 items 2 to 3 and 6, and the `candidateIndex` chain of 0051 item 1). A retry on another account of the same candidate is not a step of the walk. `walkStateOf` is the one door that turns a recorded attempt into those two `bind()` options; the write gate and doctor `mutating-assignment-binding-snapshot` both recompute through it, so a fallback attempt (`-fb`) is checked against the walk it was bound in. The write gate compares executor, pool, tier and posture. A unit record written before bindings carried a pool has no walk state this code reads: its bindings are left out and the walk restarts at the primary. **A pool is usable** when the lease can serve it: a pool with accounts needs an enabled account holding a login store for the CLI the chosen invocation declares (`credentialStore.use`, RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)); a pool with no account in either inventory is usable only as the family-named pool (the executor's own login). This reads config only (`poolUnusableReason`), so `bind()` stays pure; quarantine and leases are the lease's business at dispatch. An unusable entry is out of the candidates with `pool-unusable`, and `fgos dispatch explain` says why. **Missing cell.** An out-of-process agent seat whose family has no cell at the tier it runs at refuses `tier-cell-missing`: `no model for tier "" under family "" (runner.modelPolicies..)`, one text built by `tierCellMissingDetail` for `bind()` and for the assignment policy (which raises `tier-cell-missing: `). The older fallthrough to `executor.model` or the CLI default is deleted. When several `prefer` families exist, or in a walk, a family with no cell is skipped and recorded in `provenance.skipped`, and the refusal names the last skipped cell when nothing is left; a lone candidate refuses at once. **Lease, state and quarantine are per pool.** A seat bound to a pool leases from it: the state key is `legacyStateKey(pool)`, so the family-named pool keeps the key it always had (`openai` is `openai-codex`) and existing state, sticky records and quarantines still apply; a quarantine or fault on one pool does not touch another pool of the same family. The accounts of a pool come from `runner.llmAccounts.` when it declares the pool, else from `runner.providers..accounts`: **the transition read** (`providerAccountInventory`), which goes, together with the `runner.providers` key, once every fgOS release on the machine reads `runner.llmAccounts` (the later step that deletes `runner.providers` from the global config). `compareWithLegacyInventory` and doctor `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` go with it. **Account order is the declared order.** `rankProviderAccounts` takes the account the assignment already holds while it is usable, else the pool's accounts in the key order of the config, skipping quarantined and `disabled` ones; load does not reorder, so the first account takes every lease until it cannot (least-lease and least-recently-used are deleted from the ranking; `lastSelectedAt` is still written for `inspect`). An account id of digits only is refused (a JS object lists such a key first and would reorder the list). The lease receives the CLI from the launched invocation's declared login store (the pinned invocation, else the executor's first `cli` invocation), and `inspectAccountRotation` counts the enabled accounts of the pool for rotation. **Pin.** `--account` and the `account` key of `--override` take `pool/account` (`parseAccountPin`); a bare id is refused with the form to write. The pin selects the candidate of the chosen family whose pool matches; otherwise the seat binds unpinned and `provenance.account.skipped` names why (`account-pin-other-pool`, `account-pin-no-inventory`, `account-pin-unsupported`); an unknown account of the seat's own pool refuses `account-pin-unknown` and a disabled one `account-pin-disabled`. `binding.account` is `{ pool, id }`. `fgos workflow start --account` takes the same form and checks it against the pool's inventory at start. **Reversal triggers.** (3) Declared order goes back to least-lease ranking if one account keeps hitting its quota window while others sit idle (watch: `fgos dispatch inspect --provider-capacity` shows `openLeases` and quarantines per account). (2) The tier groups change when a family's model at a tier stops being equivalent in price or quality. Primary order stays `prefer`: if one family keeps failing first for a capability, narrow its `prefer` rather than reorder primaries globally. **Not changed.** `attemptProviderCapacityFallback` (the legacy dispatch path and workflow operations that declare `policy.fallbackExecutors`) is a second walker that leases by family key without the CLI and does not use the walk; the write gate recomputes without `independentOf` and `preferIndependentOf`, so a spread-chosen primary can differ from the recompute; per-capability tier ceilings and spend tracking are not built. Component boundary: no change (`bind()` decides candidates, the lease decides accounts). - Phần chọn ghế của rule này bị D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice) thay một phần, 2026-10-20: authority đích là [seat-binding.md](../../../seat-binding/spec.md); code đổi cùng plan của nó. Chữ rule ở trên không sửa tại chỗ. - **(herdr panes open through terminal-control, 2026-10-18; the round itself moved to the run supervisor, same day).** A herdr seat no longer has a round loop in the controller: the controller prepares the attempt (brief, home, trust seed, `allocate(key = attempt id, groupKey)`), writes a `terminal`-mode envelope and hands it to the run supervisor, which opens, briefs, watches and releases the pane through `fgos-terminal-control` (`docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md` section 5.3, `docs/platform/terminal-control/spec.md`). The group key is the dispatch batch key, else the unit run id, so every attempt of one batch lands in one tab; `FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE` is an `attach` into that group. A failed or stopped attempt's pane is kept (24 hours by default; until a person closes it when `terminal.retainFailedPaneMs` is `null`) and a finished one is closed once by `release-slot`; `terminal.layout.*` and `terminal.allocationGraceMs` reach the route from the project (then global) config, and doctor's `terminal-control`, `terminal-config` and `terminal-allocations` checks show what an attempt would use. Starting a herdr server for a confined session stays in `worker-session-boot.mjs` (a server lifecycle, not a pane operation). - **(a private home belongs to its attempt, 2026-10-18; ends the confinement orphan reaper).** Only adopt's finalize-home step removes the private home of an attempt, while the attempt lock is free and its process domain is empty; the sweep (`sweepAttempts`) is adopt alone. The pane, binder and expiry rules, `bind`/`markLaunched`/`retain`, the post-probe sweep and the herdr-launch-command write are removed; a herdr-spawn launch needs an attempt id. Why: the old rules judged a home by a pid, a pane or an age, which could take the home of a worker still running (S2); one owner removes that class of fault. Left open: a dispatch outside the assignment door that dies leaves its home (named by `fgos doctor`, removed only by an explicit `doctor --fix`, never swept), and `fgos run` no longer has a startup rule for homes written with a pane binding by an older release. - **(a Unit carries its own verify and skills, verify runs bounded, and a reviewed run at rigor high or critical needs a family per seat, 2026-10-18; owner decisions 2026-10-18; the rigor part supersedes decision 0055 for `reviewed` only).** - **`verify` stays on the Unit.** `validateUnit` keeps `verify` (a non-empty shell command) and `skills` (a non-empty list of skill names, trimmed, de-duplicated) through validation, the units-file loader, the workflow template and the round; a registered workflow template may set both too. - **Where the verify command comes from.** `verifyCommandOf` (`patterns/reviewed.mjs`) reads the Unit's own `verify`, else its capability's `verify`, and nothing else; the `code-change` preset pins none (it used to name `npm test`, which no runner ever executed, so a reviewed run recorded a verify pass that checked nothing), and `params.verify` no longer counts. A reviewed run with no verify command still passes on its checkers but its result carries `verify: { ran: false, reason }`; a solo or panel run, which has no verify step, says nothing. - **One bounded runner.** The verify step runs through `runCommand` (`src/runner/goal-check.mjs`, the same runner `return` and `approve` use) in the Unit's worktree, for at most `runner.timeoutMs` (the existing key and default; no new key, so nothing new for setup or doctor to register). A non-zero exit, a command that could not start and one that ran past the limit are each a failed verify that becomes findings naming the status (`exited N`, `timed out after Nms`, `could not run`) and the last twenty lines of output; none of them hangs the run. - **One-liner flags.** `fgos run "" --input , --verify ""` set the Unit's `inputs` and `verify`; both are refused beside `--unit` or `--resume`, and an empty value is refused before any unit run exists. - **Skills reach `bind()`.** `bind()` skips an executor whose `supports.skills` (new optional key in the executor's `supports` block, a non-empty array of names) does not list every skill the Unit names; none left refuses with reason `skills-unavailable` naming the missing skills, and the session lead never takes over such a Unit inline. Only roles that do the Unit's work are asked for skills: checker, panel and debate roles (`reviewer`, `red-team`, `tester`, `panelist*`, `synthesizer`, `thesis`, `antithesis`, `judge`) are chosen on independence alone. An executor that declares no `supports.skills` provides none. `fgos doctor` check `executor-skills-installed` fails when a declared skill has no `SKILL.md` in its runtime's skill directory of the main checkout (by each invocation's CLI: `claude` reads `.claude/skills/`, `codex` `.agents/skills/`, `omp` `.omp/skills/`, `pi` `.pi/skills/`, `grok` `.grok/skills/`, and an executor passes only when every invocation's directory has the skill; `ak:cook` is the directory `ak-cook`); `worktreeSetup.commands` copies the untracked `ak-*` skill directories from the main checkout into each new worktree, so a worker sees them. `fgos worktree create` records what its provisioning placed (`provisionWorktree` in `src/runner/worktree.mjs`: every new untracked or ignored path, with a content digest for a file and the target for a symlink, and the `node_modules` it installed declared regenerable) in `/worktree-provisioning/.json`, bound to the checkout directory's device and inode. `fgos worktree remove` moves exactly those bytes into a sibling directory before the Git port's clean check (`setProvisionedAside`): a copy only while it still matches its digest, and a recorded directory only once it is empty. It moves them back when the port refuses and deletes them, with the record, once the port has removed the checkout. A worker-edited copy or any byte the record does not name stays in place, and the port refuses on it. The brief for an `ak:cook` worker is `core/skills/_shared/ak-cook-worker-contract.md`. - **`docs:write`** is a curated capability slot (`DEFAULT_CAPABILITY_SLOTS`, description-only, `serves: { outputKind: change, domain: docs, mutates: true }`) next to `code:implement`, so `fgos setup` declares the capability the one-liner and `fgos-run` name for documentation work. - **Rigor high or critical: every seat of a `reviewed` run on its own family.** When the Unit's rigor, or its capability's rigor floor (the stronger of the two, as `bind()` computes it), is `high` or `critical`, each checker is `independentOf` the producer and of every other checker (`requiresDistinctFamilies`), a fallback walk after a provider limit re-reads that list so the replacement keeps the property, and a pool without enough families refuses the seat that cannot be placed with the existing reason `independence`. Standard and low keep the old rule (checker differs from the producer only). Decision 0055's soft spread is unchanged for `panel`: seat count there is still not capped by family count (owner, 2026-10-11). - **`debate`: two sides soft, the judge hard.** `runDebate` (`patterns/debate.mjs`) dispatches `thesis` and `antithesis` read-only with `preferIndependentOf` each other (a shared family is reported, not refused), optionally a second round where each side gets only the other's round-1 result in `inputs`, then `judge` with `independentOf: [thesis, antithesis]` and every result as `inputs`. The judge's family differing from both sides is the one hard independence rule of the pattern; an unseatable judge is bind()'s named `independence` refusal (`policy-refusal` outcome), never a same-family ruling. The three roles are listed once, in `CHECKER_ROLES` of `bind.mjs`, so they never run inline or in-process and are not asked for the Unit's skills. `fgos doctor`'s pool-independence check drives the same pattern code, so a pool with too few families fails it before a run. `unit-summary` gives the sides seat kind `producer` and the judge `judge`.
textCatalog.299c5b49c98df16010e0ac6cfc38a3a77e93bc6b:
- **RUL77 ([ĐÃ BỊ THAY phần "each door carries one posture lane" bởi RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed), decision 0062 — posture now comes from the Unit's `writes` plus the capability; "an agent executor declares no `for`" stands] posture belongs to the capability, an agent executor declares no `for`, and each door carries one posture lane; supersedes RUL76 (`execute --for ` with a "must declare" gate), 2026-10-13).** An agent executor can do any kind of work, so no `for` list describes it, and a list on one was read as the posture of every dispatch to it (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` already said a direct executor call must carry a capability anchor and never infer the minimum from `executor.for`). `resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints` reads `for` from tool executors only; on an agent executor it is inert (config still loads, so projects and worktrees that carry one keep dispatching) and `fgos doctor` names it under `executor-profile-warnings` (`executor..agent-for-inert`); the agent executors' `for` lists are gone from this repo's `.fgos/config.json` (`decide --for` routing unchanged: it reads `capabilities..prefer`). The CLI door `execute ` refuses before spawning when no `--for` is given (`capability-required`, listing the writing capabilities and the read-only door); programmatic callers (Assignment, Work) pass their own capability hints and are unchanged. `execute --for ` runs the invocation that capability `prefer`s for that executor, else the first plain cli invocation with no sandbox backend, instead of always the first cli invocation. That door leases no provider account, so it carries writing work only: a capability with required confinement is refused (`posture-needs-assignment`). Read-only work runs sandboxed as a Workflow unit with `writes: []` (`fgos workflow start --units`), which binds the read-only posture and leases the account (the architecture-advisory seats ran that way: `confined-bwrap`, login provisioned); `execute --contract --executor ` keeps a named provider and leases its account but runs unconfined, read-only by instruction only (measured: `execute openai --for code:review` on the bare door ran `codex-cli-bwrap` confined and got 401 with no login; the same read through `--contract --executor openai` answered, on `cli-spawn` with `confinement: null`). A sandboxed read-only door that also keeps a named provider does not exist yet. The calling agent answers Q1 (does it write? does a provider matter?) from prose doctrine in `core/skills/_shared/capability-matching.md`, with no classifier or workflow generator. Decided after an `architecture-advisory` run (`wf-run-1791875339761-10315b91`: framing and shaping with three blind seats and a synthesizer completed; critique was blocked by a Codex trust prompt, so no reviewed synthesis exists). Not built: a soft provider hint on `decide` (`--prefer`, the synthesizer's recommendation) — naming the executor on `execute` already lets a caller pick a provider, and the hint would change `bind()`, shared with Workflow binding; revisit when a caller needs "this provider if it can, else any". Since 2026-10-14 (RUL88 (ad-hoc Unit prefer and persona, the one-liner), decision 0061) that hint exists on the Unit, not on `decide`: `fgos run "" --provider ` and an ad-hoc Unit's `prefer` try the provider first and fail over into the pool, and a read-only one-liner is the sandboxed read-only door that keeps a preferred provider. 1. **Account lock.** One kernel mutex per provider account, machine scope, at `/locks/provider-account//.lock` through holder-lock, separate from the state lock (`provider-state.lock`). A waiter waits with timers, never by blocking the event loop (panel seats share a process and may share an account); a caller that must not wait (a removal) tries once. The renewal or unlock-probe call runs through the lock (`spawnHolding`, i.e. `runBorrowed`), so a dead holder with a live call keeps the lock and a second renewal never redeems the same refresh token; the lock is released only after the call and every process it started have exited. The account directory `/account-locks///` still holds the pending copies, the scratch home and the cooldown. 2. **Refresh-ahead.** After the final account selection (the executor-fallback lease included) and before a confined private home is built from it, when the login has less than the window left, fgOS renews it once. The window is `max(60 minutes, probe timeout + 5 minutes)`. Only the entry of the dispatched provider counts, for the window and for "was it renewed" (Codex: its single entry; pi: the key equal to the provider id or starting with `-`; omp: the row `provider` likewise; a lone oauth entry of another provider is not used; zero or several matches skip the renewal as `entry-unidentified`), so an abandoned login of another provider never makes every dispatch renew, and only that entry is made due and applied. Under the account lock it applies any leftover copy first, re-reads the source, and skips for 30 minutes after a failed renewal; then it builds a scratch home under the account directory (mode 0700, the listed files only), makes only that copy look due, runs the layout's probe call on it (wrapped in coreutils `timeout --kill-after=5`, so the child ends on its own even if the runner dies and the account lock does not outlive it unbounded; the runner's own timer stays; the lazy-probe unlock call, an account locked for a dead login, is wrapped the same way), and applies the renewed entry to the real store. The real store is never made to look expired, so the owner's own CLI does not renew because of this, a failed or hung call leaves it untouched, and a scratch copy left by a dead runner is applied (if newer) by the next lock holder and then removed. Where each layout keeps its expiry: pi `auth.json` `.expires` (ms; seconds below 1e12), `type: oauth` entries only; omp `agent.db` table `auth_credentials`, `data.expires` (ms), rows `credential_type = 'oauth'` and no `disabled_cause`; Codex `auth.json`, due at the earlier of the access token's `exp` claim and `last_refresh` plus 8 days (`TOKEN_REFRESH_INTERVAL`, `should_refresh_proactively` in `codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs` of openai/codex; the same file renews at five minutes before `exp` when the token can be read). A layout that cannot be read (an API key, agy, no `node:sqlite`) is left as it was. 3. **Apply (compare-before-write).** Shared by refresh-ahead and write-back, always under the account lock: only an entry whose expiry is strictly later than the source's and whose refresh token differs from the source's replaces it (compared in memory, never printed; a copy that still holds the source's refresh token renewed nothing), and for a fresh renewal the new expiry must also be in the future, while a copy staged earlier (a pane's home, a pending or leftover copy) is applied even if its access token has expired since, because its refresh token is the newer one and the source's is already spent, only that entry changes (other pi providers, other omp rows and columns, other Codex fields stay as they were), a copy that cannot be read, has an unexpected shape, or has no refresh token where the source's entry has one never touches the source. A copy is deleted only when the source was read successfully and proves the copy is not newer (same refresh token, or an expiry not strictly later), or when the copy is proven malformed (corrupt JSON, or it parses to no usable entry, or it has no store file); when the source is unreadable or half-written, the entry cannot be identified at apply time, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass (`node:sqlite` unavailable, a database that will not open), the copy is kept (a fresh scratch copy moves to `pending/`) and the result is `apply-deferred`, never `applied` or `not-renewed`. An operating-system read error on a copy file (permissions, I/O) is reported as `unreadable-file` and keeps the copy (`apply-deferred`); only a store file that is not there (`missing-file`) is proven empty. pi and Codex files are replaced through a temp file and a rename, recomputed when the source changed in between; the omp store is changed by a row update in one transaction, never by replacing the file the owner's omp may hold open. 4. **Write-back at removal.** When a dispatch opted in, the private home's ownership marker records `credentialWriteBack` (provider, account, source home, layout, runtime dir; names and paths only). One removal function serves the driver cleanup, the finalizer of a settled dispatch and the orphan reaper: before deleting a home whose marker asks for it, a login in the home that is newer than the source's is staged under `pending/` (atomic rename) and applied under the account lock, tried once without waiting; when the lock is busy, or nothing proves the copy is not newer (the source is unreadable, its entry cannot be identified, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass, such as `node:sqlite` being unavailable: an omp store is then staged as plain files, write-ahead log included), it stays pending and the next refresh-ahead (or removal) applies it once it can be identified, even if the source still looks fresh, because the source's own refresh token may already be spent; a refresh-ahead that skips because the entry is unidentified applies the pending copies too, so the ones that have become identifiable clear. Pending copies are limited to five per login store (per account for a single-store account, per `stores/` for a per-CLI one), but only redundant ones are ever dropped: after the pending copies were applied, under the account lock, a copy whose logins are identical to another pending copy's (compared in memory by entry key, refresh token and expiry, or by the bytes of the store files and of a non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal when a copy cannot be parsed; never printed) is dropped, oldest first, while the account is over the limit, and the newest of each identical group stays; a drop writes one stderr line `credential-pending-dropped` with a count only. A copy that cannot be shown redundant, or obsolete by the source, is never dropped to make room, so an account can stay over the limit, and the doctor check reports it. A staged copy and the pending directory are synced to disk before the home goes. A copy a probe left half-written (pi rewrites its store in place; omp commits row updates in a database transaction) is kept under `torn/` for hand recovery, never applied or dropped automatically, and reported by the doctor check at any age. This covers the probe's scratch copy only: a scratch home a dead runner left, and a pane home whose store was cut off, are still removed when their JSON cannot be read. A pane home whose store files are byte for byte the source's, with no non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal on either side (a login renewed before a checkpoint sits only there; a zero-byte or missing one counts as none, the shared-memory index counts for nothing, and one that cannot be read, other than as missing, is never taken for none), renewed nothing and is not staged, parsable or not. If staging itself fails, the private home and its marker are kept (the removal reports failure, one stderr line with a fixed code and no path or value) so a later removal, the reaper's included, retries; only a copy proven malformed, or one the source was read to prove not newer, lets the home go. Each failed attempt is counted in the marker (`credentialKept`: attempts, first time, time of the last counted attempt; failures less than 15 minutes after the last counted one are not counted again, so a transient fault does not use the budget up); the marker is rewritten through a temp file and a rename, and a marker that is present but unreadable stops the removal. After five attempts the home is held: no further removal attempt and no deletion by age, however old. A held home is re-checked, under the account lock, when that account is next renewed (the temp roots searched are the same as doctor's: the default one plus each registered backend's own `tempRoot`; a home under a backend's separate `privateHomeRoot` is in none of them, so no check, repair, reaper or renewal sees it, and it is never deleted either) and by `fgos doctor --fix`, and only a home of the lock's own runtime directory: it is removed only when the source is readable and proves its login is not newer, or when that login can now be staged beside the source (and is applied); otherwise it stays held. A marker file that is no recognisable marker at all (not JSON, not an object, no contract name) stops any removal of its home. The finalizer compares the ownership marker's digest without `credentialKept` (a failed driver cleanup adds it after the digest was taken) and carries on with the dispatch's other resources past a home that cannot go (the dispatch is recorded as retained, with the home's reason). The doctor check `credential-copies-retained` reports, by provider and account, held homes (a failure, naming the home directory), homes still being retried and pending or scratch copies older than a day (warnings), with counts, ages and never a value; the check deletes nothing. Any other write-back problem is reported on stderr by a fixed code and never stops the removal. 5. **Known exposure.** Refresh-ahead can spend the refresh token that a pane started just outside the window still holds: that pane's own renewal is then refused, no worse than before this rule, and write-back cannot rescue it because its renewal failed. A run that copied the login with more than the window left and runs longer than that remainder is the case. 6. **No value in any output.** Results, events, markers, cooldown and lock records, stderr and reports carry fixed codes (`unreadable-json`, `unexpected-shape`, `sqlite-unavailable`, ...) and fingerprints at most, never a token or a parser message (which quotes nearby input). - **RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store, 2026-10-13).** A herdr pane with a private home carries the login of the account the capacity layer leased (RUL65b), but the folder-trust seed (`seedWorkspaceTrust`, `trustStorePaths` in `src/runner/dispatch/herdr-round.mjs`) derived the trust decision from the store of the account the invocation's static env names (`codex-herdr-fgovn`: `CODEX_HOME=${HOME}/.codex-fgovn`). It leases, spawns and writes nothing. - Phần chọn ghế của rule này bị D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice) thay một phần, 2026-10-20: authority đích là [seat-binding.md](../../../seat-binding/spec.md); code đổi cùng plan của nó. Chữ rule ở trên không sửa tại chỗ. - **RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat; a capability's own rigor raises its own ceiling, 2026-10-17).** `runner.maxTier`, when set, is the highest tier a seat runs at, whatever asked for the tier: the unit's rigor, the capability's rigor floor, or an override (`--override '{"tier":...}'`). Mechanism and tables: [run-supervisor spec, section 9.1](../../../run-supervisor/spec.md#91-controller-death). - **RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads; the driver hands over exactly that store's files, 2026-10-19).** A confined `cli` invocation may declare `credentialStore: { use, homeEnv, files? }` in the config: `use` is the store key (`codex`, `pi`, `omp`, a lowercase key; it replaces the basename of `command` as the key into an account's `credentialSources`), `homeEnv` is the environment variable its CLI reads its login home from, and `files` (optional, non-empty, relative, no `..`, no repeats) lists what to hand over. The bwrap driver points `env[homeEnv]` at the private home (over a value the invocation's own `env` carries, which names the real store) and copies the files of the store: the invocation's `files`, else the leased account's list (`home-files`), else `auth.json` (`codex-home`). **The copy rule replaces "a missing file refuses the launch":** files that are present are copied, an absent one is left out, and a store with none present refuses the launch with `credential-provisioning` (`credential-store-empty`, naming the account, the store key and the home); a dangling link, a link out of the home, a non-regular file or a path with `..` still refuses, as before. **An invocation that declares no store gets no login and no home variable, whatever account was leased** (the lesson of `569f72d3b`, which copied a Codex login into every executor's home), and `assessBwrap` refuses a policy that grants no `private-home` to an invocation that reads a store. The soft spread stays active in a walk and ranks the passing candidates, ties falling to walk order; without a spread request the walk takes the first untried candidate. **`runner.tierFallback`** is `{ : [family, ...] }` with the tiers of `modelPolicies`, each a non-empty list of distinct family names (the `modelPolicies` key, so GLM is `z-ai`); `validateTierFallbackShape` refuses anything else at load naming the key path, `tierFallbackOf` reads it, and doctor `tier-fallback` warns on a listed family with no cell at that tier or no agent executor. The code enforces the tier boundary and the narrowing only; the owner's groups are configuration: doer tiers (nano, standard, advanced) fall back across gemini, deepseek, z-ai, then claude, openai; flagship and frontier across claude, openai, gemini and xai. The write gate compares executor, pool, tier and posture. This reads config only (`poolUnusableReason`), so `bind()` stays pure; quarantine and leases are the lease's business at dispatch. An unusable entry is out of the candidates with `pool-unusable`, and `fgos dispatch explain` says why. **Missing cell.** An out-of-process agent seat whose family has no cell at the tier it runs at refuses `tier-cell-missing`: `no model for tier "" under family "" (runner.modelPolicies..)`, one text built by `tierCellMissingDetail` for `bind()` and for the assignment policy (which raises `tier-cell-missing: `). The older fallthrough to `executor.model` or the CLI default is deleted. When several `prefer` families exist, or in a walk, a family with no cell is skipped and recorded in `provenance.skipped`, and the refusal names the last skipped cell when nothing is left; a lone candidate refuses at once. **Lease, state and quarantine are per pool.** A seat bound to a pool leases from it: the state key is `legacyStateKey(pool)`, so the family-named pool keeps the key it always had (`openai` is `openai-codex`) and existing state, sticky records and quarantines still apply; a quarantine or fault on one pool does not touch another pool of the same family. The accounts of a pool come from `runner.llmAccounts.` when it declares the pool, else from `runner.providers..accounts`: **the transition read** (`providerAccountInventory`), which goes, together with the `runner.providers` key, once every fgOS release on the machine reads `runner.llmAccounts` (the later step that deletes `runner.providers` from the global config). `compareWithLegacyInventory` and doctor `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` go with it. **Account order is the declared order.** `rankProviderAccounts` takes the account the assignment already holds while it is usable, else the pool's accounts in the key order of the config, skipping quarantined and `disabled` ones; load does not reorder, so the first account takes every lease until it cannot (least-lease and least-recently-used are deleted from the ranking; `lastSelectedAt` is still written for `inspect`). An account id of digits only is refused (a JS object lists such a key first and would reorder the list). The lease receives the CLI from the launched invocation's declared login store (the pinned invocation, else the executor's first `cli` invocation), and `inspectAccountRotation` counts the enabled accounts of the pool for rotation. **Pin.** `--account` and the `account` key of `--override` take `pool/account` (`parseAccountPin`); a bare id is refused with the form to write. The pin selects the candidate of the chosen family whose pool matches; otherwise the seat binds unpinned and `provenance.account.skipped` names why (`account-pin-other-pool`, `account-pin-no-inventory`, `account-pin-unsupported`); an unknown account of the seat's own pool refuses `account-pin-unknown` and a disabled one `account-pin-disabled`. `binding.account` is `{ pool, id }`. `fgos workflow start --account` takes the same form and checks it against the pool's inventory at start. **Reversal triggers.** (3) Declared order goes back to least-lease ranking if one account keeps hitting its quota window while others sit idle (watch: `fgos dispatch inspect --provider-capacity` shows `openLeases` and quarantines per account).
