Component boundary: no change (`bind()` decides candidates, the lease decides accounts). - Phần chọn ghế của rule này bị D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice) thay một phần, 2026-10-20: authority đích là [seat-binding.md](../../../seat-binding/spec.md); code đổi cùng plan của nó. Chữ rule ở trên không sửa tại chỗ. - **(herdr panes open through terminal-control, 2026-10-18; the round itself moved to the run supervisor, same day).** A herdr seat no longer has a round loop in the controller: the controller prepares the attempt (brief, home, trust seed, `allocate(key = attempt id, groupKey)`), writes a `terminal`-mode envelope and hands it to the run supervisor, which opens, briefs, watches and releases the pane through `fgos-terminal-control` (`docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md` section 5.3, `docs/platform/terminal-control/spec.md`). The group key is the dispatch batch key, else the unit run id, so every attempt of one batch lands in one tab; `FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE` is an `attach` into that group. A failed or stopped attempt's pane is kept until a person closes it (a positive `terminal.retainFailedPaneMs` only makes doctor report the pane with its pane id once that time has passed; nothing closes it) and a finished one is closed once by `release-slot`; `terminal.layout.*` and `terminal.allocationGraceMs` reach the route from the project (then global) config, and doctor's `terminal-control` and `terminal-allocations` checks show what an attempt would use. Starting a herdr server for a confined session stays in `worker-session-boot.mjs` (a server lifecycle, not a pane operation). - **(a private home belongs to its attempt, 2026-10-18; ends the confinement orphan reaper).** Only adopt's finalize-home step removes the private home of an attempt, while the attempt lock is free and its process domain is empty; the sweep (`sweepAttempts`) is adopt alone. The pane, binder and expiry rules, `bind`/`markLaunched`/`retain`, the post-probe sweep and the herdr-launch-command write are removed; a herdr-spawn launch needs an attempt id. Why: the old rules judged a home by a pid, a pane or an age, which could take the home of a worker still running (S2); one owner removes that class of fault. Left open: a dispatch outside the assignment door that dies leaves its home (named by `fgos doctor`, removed only by an explicit `doctor --fix`, never swept), and `fgos run` no longer has a startup rule for homes written with a pane binding by an older release. - **(a Unit carries its own verify and skills, verify runs bounded, and a reviewed run at rigor high or critical needs a family per seat, 2026-10-18; owner decisions 2026-10-18; the rigor part supersedes decision 0055 for `reviewed` only).** - **`verify` stays on the Unit.** `validateUnit` keeps `verify` (a non-empty shell command) and `skills` (a non-empty list of skill names, trimmed, de-duplicated) through validation, the units-file loader, the workflow template and the round; a registered workflow template may set both too. - **Where the verify command comes from.** `verifyCommandOf` (`patterns/reviewed.mjs`) reads the Unit's own `verify`, else its capability's `verify`, and nothing else; the `code-change` preset pins none (it used to name `npm test`, which no runner ever executed, so a reviewed run recorded a verify pass that checked nothing), and `params.verify` no longer counts. A reviewed run with no verify command still passes on its checkers but its result carries `verify: { ran: false, reason }`; a solo or panel run, which has no verify step, says nothing. - **One bounded runner.** The verify step runs through `runCommand` (`src/runner/goal-check.mjs`, the same runner `return` and `approve` use) in the Unit's worktree, for at most `runner.timeoutMs` (the existing key and default; no new key, so nothing new for setup or doctor to register). A non-zero exit, a command that could not start and one that ran past the limit are each a failed verify that becomes findings naming the status (`exited N`, `timed out after Nms`, `could not run`) and the last twenty lines of output; none of them hangs the run. - **One-liner flags.** `fgos run "" --input , --verify ""` set the Unit's `inputs` and `verify`; both are refused beside `--unit` or `--resume`, and an empty value is refused before any unit run exists. - **Skills reach `bind()`.** `bind()` skips an executor whose `supports.skills` (new optional key in the executor's `supports` block, a non-empty array of names) does not list every skill the Unit names; none left refuses with reason `skills-unavailable` naming the missing skills, and the session lead never takes over such a Unit inline. Only roles that do the Unit's work are asked for skills: checker, panel and debate roles (`reviewer`, `red-team`, `tester`, `panelist*`, `synthesizer`, `thesis`, `antithesis`, `judge`) are chosen on independence alone. An executor that declares no `supports.skills` provides none. `fgos doctor` check `executor-skills-installed` fails when a declared skill has no `SKILL.md` in its runtime's skill directory of the main checkout (by each invocation's CLI: `claude` reads `.claude/skills/`, `codex` `.agents/skills/`, `omp` `.omp/skills/`, `pi` `.pi/skills/`, `grok` `.grok/skills/`, and an executor passes only when every invocation's directory has the skill; `ak:cook` is the directory `ak-cook`); `worktreeSetup.commands` copies the untracked `ak-*` skill directories from the main checkout into each new worktree, so a worker sees them. `fgos worktree create` records what its provisioning placed (`provisionWorktree` in `src/runner/worktree.mjs`: every new untracked or ignored path, with a content digest for a file and the target for a symlink, and the `node_modules` it installed declared regenerable) in `/worktree-provisioning/.json`, bound to the checkout directory's device and inode. `fgos worktree remove` moves exactly those bytes into a sibling directory before the Git port's clean check (`setProvisionedAside`): a copy only while it still matches its digest, and a recorded directory only once it is empty. It moves them back when the port refuses and deletes them, with the record, once the port has removed the checkout. A worker-edited copy or any byte the record does not name stays in place, and the port refuses on it. The brief for an `ak:cook` worker is `core/skills/_shared/ak-cook-worker-contract.md`. - **`docs:write`** is a curated capability slot (`DEFAULT_CAPABILITY_SLOTS`, description-only, `serves: { outputKind: change, domain: docs, mutates: true }`) next to `code:implement`, so `fgos setup` declares the capability the one-liner and `fgos-run` name for documentation work. - **Rigor high or critical: every seat of a `reviewed` run on its own family.** When the Unit's rigor, or its capability's rigor floor (the stronger of the two, as `bind()` computes it), is `high` or `critical`, each checker is `independentOf` the producer and of every other checker (`requiresDistinctFamilies`), a fallback walk after a provider limit re-reads that list so the replacement keeps the property, and a pool without enough families refuses the seat that cannot be placed with the existing reason `independence`. Standard and low keep the old rule (checker differs from the producer only). Decision 0055's soft spread is unchanged for `panel`: seat count there is still not capped by family count (owner, 2026-10-11). - **`debate`: two sides soft, the judge hard.** `runDebate` (`patterns/debate.mjs`) dispatches `thesis` and `antithesis` read-only with `preferIndependentOf` each other (a shared family is reported, not refused), optionally a second round where each side gets only the other's round-1 result in `inputs`, then `judge` with `independentOf: [thesis, antithesis]` and every result as `inputs`. The judge's family differing from both sides is the one hard independence rule of the pattern; an unseatable judge is bind()'s named `independence` refusal (`policy-refusal` outcome), never a same-family ruling. The three roles are listed once, in `CHECKER_ROLES` of `bind.mjs`, so they never run inline or in-process and are not asked for the Unit's skills. `fgos doctor`'s pool-independence check drives the same pattern code, so a pool with too few families fails it before a run. `unit-summary` gives the sides seat kind `producer` and the judge `judge`.

- **RUL77 ([ĐÃ BỊ THAY phần "each door carries one posture lane" bởi RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed), decision 0062 — posture now comes from the Unit's `writes` plus the capability; "an agent executor declares no `for`" stands] posture belongs to the capability, an agent executor declares no `for`, and each door carries one posture lane; supersedes RUL76 (`execute --for ` with a "must declare" gate), 2026-10-13).** An agent executor can do any kind of work, so no `for` list describes it, and a list on one was read as the posture of every dispatch to it (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` already said a direct executor call must carry a capability anchor and never infer the minimum from `executor.for`). `resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints` reads `for` from tool executors only; on an agent executor it is inert (config still loads, so projects and worktrees that carry one keep dispatching) and `fgos doctor` names it under `executor-profile-warnings` (`executor..agent-for-inert`); the agent executors' `for` lists are gone from this repo's `.fgos/config.json` (`decide --for` routing unchanged: it reads `capabilities..prefer`). The CLI door `execute ` refuses before spawning when no `--for` is given (`capability-required`, listing the writing capabilities and the read-only door); programmatic callers (Assignment, Work) pass their own capability hints and are unchanged. `execute --for ` runs the invocation that capability `prefer`s for that executor, else the first plain cli invocation with no sandbox backend, instead of always the first cli invocation. That door leases no provider account, so it carries writing work only: a capability with required confinement is refused (`posture-needs-assignment`). Read-only work runs sandboxed as a Workflow unit with `writes: []` (`fgos workflow start --units`), which binds the read-only posture and leases the account (the architecture-advisory seats ran that way: `confined-bwrap`, login provisioned); `execute --contract --executor ` keeps a named provider and leases its account but runs unconfined, read-only by instruction only (measured: `execute openai --for code:review` on the bare door ran `codex-cli-bwrap` confined and got 401 with no login; the same read through `--contract --executor openai` answered, on `cli-spawn` with `confinement: null`). A sandboxed read-only door that also keeps a named provider does not exist yet. The calling agent answers Q1 (does it write? does a provider matter?) from prose doctrine in `core/skills/_shared/capability-matching.md`, with no classifier or workflow generator. Decided after an `architecture-advisory` run (`wf-run-1791875339761-10315b91`: framing and shaping with three blind seats and a synthesizer completed; critique was blocked by a Codex trust prompt, so no reviewed synthesis exists). Not built: a soft provider hint on `decide` (`--prefer`, the synthesizer's recommendation) — naming the executor on `execute` already lets a caller pick a provider, and the hint would change `bind()`, shared with Workflow binding; revisit when a caller needs "this provider if it can, else any". Since 2026-10-14 (RUL88 (ad-hoc Unit prefer and persona, the one-liner), decision 0061) that hint exists on the Unit, not on `decide`: `fgos run "" --provider ` and an ad-hoc Unit's `prefer` try the provider first and fail over into the pool, and a read-only one-liner is the sandboxed read-only door that keeps a preferred provider. 1. **Account lock.** One kernel mutex per provider account, machine scope, at `/locks/provider-account//.lock` through holder-lock, separate from the state lock (`provider-state.lock`). A waiter waits with timers, never by blocking the event loop (panel seats share a process and may share an account); a caller that must not wait (a removal) tries once. The renewal or unlock-probe call runs through the lock (`spawnHolding`, i.e. `runBorrowed`), so a dead holder with a live call keeps the lock and a second renewal never redeems the same refresh token; the lock is released only after the call and every process it started have exited. The account directory `/account-locks///` still holds the pending copies, the scratch home and the cooldown. 2. **Refresh-ahead.** After the final account selection (the executor-fallback lease included) and before a confined private home is built from it, when the login has less than the window left, fgOS renews it once. Only roles that do the Unit's work are asked for skills: checker, panel and debate roles (`reviewer`, `red-team`, `tester`, `panelist*`, `synthesizer`, `thesis`, `antithesis`, `judge`) are chosen on independence alone. An executor that declares no `supports.skills` provides none. `fgos doctor` check `executor-skills-installed` fails when a declared skill has no `SKILL.md` in its runtime's skill directory of the main checkout (by each invocation's CLI: `claude` reads `.claude/skills/`, `codex` `.agents/skills/`, `omp` `.omp/skills/`, `pi` `.pi/skills/`, `grok` `.grok/skills/`, and an executor passes only when every invocation's directory has the skill; `ak:cook` is the directory `ak-cook`); `worktreeSetup.commands` copies the untracked `ak-*` skill directories from the main checkout into each new worktree, so a worker sees them. `fgos worktree create` records what its provisioning placed (`provisionWorktree` in `src/runner/worktree.mjs`: every new untracked or ignored path, with a content digest for a file and the target for a symlink, and the `node_modules` it installed declared regenerable) in `/worktree-provisioning/.json`, bound to the checkout directory's device and inode. `fgos worktree remove` moves exactly those bytes into a sibling directory before the Git port's clean check (`setProvisionedAside`): a copy only while it still matches its digest, and a recorded directory only once it is empty. It moves them back when the port refuses and deletes them, with the record, once the port has removed the checkout. A worker-edited copy or any byte the record does not name stays in place, and the port refuses on it. The brief for an `ak:cook` worker is `core/skills/_shared/ak-cook-worker-contract.md`. - **`docs:write`** is a curated capability slot (`DEFAULT_CAPABILITY_SLOTS`, description-only, `serves: { outputKind: change, domain: docs, mutates: true }`) next to `code:implement`, so `fgos setup` declares the capability the one-liner and `fgos-run` name for documentation work. - **Rigor high or critical: every seat of a `reviewed` run on its own family.** When the Unit's rigor, or its capability's rigor floor (the stronger of the two, as `bind()` computes it), is `high` or `critical`, each checker is `independentOf` the producer and of every other checker (`requiresDistinctFamilies`), a fallback walk after a provider limit re-reads that list so the replacement keeps the property, and a pool without enough families refuses the seat that cannot be placed with the existing reason `independence`. Standard and low keep the old rule (checker differs from the producer only). Decision 0055's soft spread is unchanged for `panel`: seat count there is still not capped by family count (owner, 2026-10-11). - **`debate`: two sides soft, the judge hard.** `runDebate` (`patterns/debate.mjs`) dispatches `thesis` and `antithesis` read-only with `preferIndependentOf` each other (a shared family is reported, not refused), optionally a second round where each side gets only the other's round-1 result in `inputs`, then `judge` with `independentOf: [thesis, antithesis]` and every result as `inputs`. The judge's family differing from both sides is the one hard independence rule of the pattern; an unseatable judge is bind()'s named `independence` refusal (`policy-refusal` outcome), never a same-family ruling. The three roles are listed once, in `CHECKER_ROLES` of `bind.mjs`, so they never run inline or in-process and are not asked for the Unit's skills. `fgos doctor`'s pool-independence check drives the same pattern code, so a pool with too few families fails it before a run. `unit-summary` gives the sides seat kind `producer` and the judge `judge`.
textCatalog.3da8f76a87a4b308e36b4f9dbb3605cd17249d22:
- **RUL101 (the per-worktree dispatch lock is a kernel lock held through holder-lock; a dead holder releases at once, 2026-10-16).** The lock a dispatch takes on its working directory (`dispatch-cwd`, rank 30, kind `lease`, scope still `fgosDir`) is a kernel lock on an open file description, acquired through the holder-lock facade (`src/holder-lock/`, authority `docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md`), with the cwd keyed by `dev:ino` after `realpath`. The lock file is `<fgosDir>/locks/dispatch-cwd--<dev>-<ino>.lock`, so one directory reached through a symlink is one lock; a cwd that does not exist fails as `worker-spawn-fail` before any lock. There is no holder record, no `ttlMs`, no heartbeat renewal and no reclaim by a contender: the kernel releases the lock when every process holding the description has died, so a holder killed without releasing, with or without a reused pid, blocks nobody; a live holder that is wedged keeps it until it exits. `sharedCwd` and `forceSharedCwd` still take no lock. A second dispatch on a held cwd fails `dispatch-in-flight` naming the holder pid. The resume guard of `fgos run --resume` and the reconcile planner read the kernel's holder list (`lockHolders`, which takes no lock) and fall back to `probe(dispatch-cwd)` (one non-blocking shared try) only where holders cannot be listed, since a shared try could make a concurrent one-try acquire see `held`; they refuse on a holder, neither judges a holder alive or dead, and a lock that cannot be read is never read as free. The legacy `.fgos/dispatch--<cwd>.lock` path is fenced by a tombstone at cutover for every worktree and claim, in both the `path.resolve` and the `realpath` form; `fgos dispatch reconcile clear-cwd-lock` only reports held or free and never clears a cwd lock. The reconcile planner's own local lock (`reconcile`, rank 80) is a kernel mutex at `<fgosDir>/locks/reconcile.lock` under the same port. Order inside one `LockScope` is enforced at acquire: a lock taken at a rank not above every rank the scope already holds throws `lock-order-violation` at once, with no trace-then-warn release.
- **RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool; one family has one executor; llmAccounts is read for checking only, 2026-10-17).** A cell of `runner.modelPolicies.<family>.<tier>` is a model, a model served by a named pool (`model@pool`), or a non-empty ordered list of those. The pool is the service provider that bills the call. A cell entry is split at its last `@`, so a model id that itself contains `@` names its pool explicitly (`claude-opus-4@20250514@vertex`); an entry without `@` is served by the pool named after the family. There is no default-pool key. A run uses the first entry served by the family's own pool (`resolveTierModel`); `resolveTierCandidates` returns every entry for `fgos dispatch explain` and doctor. An entry served by another pool is accepted and never run until the lease routes pools; a cell with no entry for the family's pool counts as a missing tier, which still falls back to the executor's own `model` or the CLI default. The project config accepts every form. The global `~/.fgos/config.json` is read by every fgOS release on the machine, and an older release fails on a list and passes `model@pool` to the CLI as a model id, so a list or `@` cell there is dropped with a warning naming the cell (once per process), and doctor `global-model-policies-portable` fails on it.
  Each agent family (`providerModel`) is served by exactly one executor; its transports (headless cli, herdr pane, sandboxed or not) are invocations of that executor, and `bind()` picks the pane invocation inside herdr and a cli one outside, so a capability gets the same family and model in both places. Doctor `executor-family-unique` fails on a family with two agent executors.
  `runner.llmAccounts.<pool>.<account>` is the machine's account inventory, global-only: `credentialStore: { <cli>: <login directory> }` (`~`, `${HOME}` and `$HOME` expand), plus optional `label` and `disabled`. A pool name is the family name for the family's own vendor and the provider's name otherwise (`openrouter`); it may not contain `@` nor be another spelling of a configured family (`codex`, `openai-codex`, `glm`, `agy`). `readLlmAccounts` reports problems instead of throwing; `compareWithLegacyInventory` sets it against `runner.providers.<provider>.accounts` by the state key the lease uses (`openai` is `openai-codex` there). The lease, account pins and credential provisioning still read `runner.providers` only. Doctor: `llm-accounts-shape` fails on any reader problem, `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` warns on accounts or login directories that differ once `llmAccounts` is declared, `model-policy-pools` warns on a cell naming a pool `llmAccounts` does not declare.
  `fgos dispatch explain --for <capability> [--rigor <r>]` binds the capability through `bind()` and reports the family and the `prefer` entry that chose it, the tier, its source (rigor, override) and its ceiling (RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat; a capability's own rigor raises its own ceiling)), the whole cell with each entry marked `used`, `fallback-same-pool` or `pending-pool-routing`, the executor and invocation, and the pool's accounts in both inventories. It leases, spawns and writes nothing.
- **RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat; a capability's own rigor raises its own ceiling, 2026-10-17).** `runner.maxTier`, when set, is the highest tier a seat runs at, whatever asked for the tier: the unit's rigor, the capability's rigor floor, or an override (`--override '{"tier":...}'`). A capability that declares its own `rigor` in `runner.capabilities` raises the ceiling for its own seats to `rigorToTier[rigor]` when that tier is higher. The ceiling of a seat is therefore the higher of `runner.maxTier` and the tier of its capability's declared rigor (`resolveTierCeiling` in `bind.mjs`); a unit's rigor and an override stay under it, so only the config decides which capabilities may run above the cap, and a frontier override on a capability declaring `high` stops at `flagship`. Without `runner.maxTier` there is no ceiling. A capability cannot be held below the global cap this way. The binding records the ceiling on `provenance.tier.ceiling` as `{ value, source }`, `source` being `global` or `capability-rigor(<capability>, <rigor>)`; a clamped tier's source reads `clamped:maxTier(<tier>, <ceiling source>)`. `fgos dispatch explain` shows the ceiling, and doctor `capability-rigor-ceiling` lists the capabilities lifted above `runner.maxTier` with the tier and model they run at; it never fails. The assignment policy (`resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy`) raises the tier `bind()` hands it and applies no ceiling, so when `bind()` clamped, the policy's recorded tier can read higher than the tier that ran; the model is always the one `bind()` chose.

textCatalog.4d0599aeabec3d9f17d933e855897f53a6ffb047:
- **Blocked when:** never — running `fgos setup` always attempts its work;
  a shell profile that does not exist is simply skipped rather than
  refused.
- **What changes:** for every shell profile the caller actually has (bash's
  and/or zsh's, whichever exist), the shell helper's source line is added
  if not already present — never duplicated on a repeat run. The local
  project config file is also brought up to date: any setting present in
  the current default schema but missing from the caller's file is added,
  without ever changing a setting the caller already customized; a config
  file that already has every current default is left untouched. The same
  fill-missing-only treatment is applied to the **global** config file
  (`~/.fgos/config.json`, tsk-1ri) — `fgos setup` initializes it with the
  same default schema the project-local file gets, or fills in any missing
  key, every time it runs, regardless of which project it's run from;
  a value the caller already customized at the global level is never
  overwritten. The lock directories of row 5g are created when missing:
  `<lockRoot>` and `<fgosDir>/locks`, both mode 0700, an existing one tightened to it (the `lock-dirs` fix);
  the `terminal` section of row 5h is one of the defaults the
  fill-missing-only merge adds; `<stateRoot>/terminal` is created with mode 0700 (the
  `terminal-dir` fix).
- **Side effects:** the caller's own shell profile file(s), local project
  config file, global config file (`~/.fgos/config.json`), and the two lock
  directories may be created or modified; nothing outside the caller's own
  environment is touched, and no network access happens.
- **Afterwards:** the caller sees exactly what changed — which profile
  file(s) gained the source line (or already had it), which project config
  settings were newly added (or that none were needed), and which global
  config settings were newly added (or that none were needed, or that the
  global file was just created). Nothing is done silently; running `fgos
  setup` again when everything is already current reports that plainly,
  without repeating any change.

- Quản lý nhật ký và vòng đời case đo lường (`fgos metrics case`).

- Quản lý store lock (`<fgosDir>/locks/observe.lock`, kernel lock của holder-lock) và phân mảnh writer shard (`.fgos/observe/<store>/<writerId>.jsonl`). `writerId` lấy từ crate Session Identity ([spec](../identity/spec.md)): chính session id khi `source` là `env`/`registry` (gồm `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, `CODEX_THREAD_ID`), `pid-<id>` khi `pid`/`unresolved` (gốc terminal hoặc session, không còn pid của chính process). `sessionId` của friction cũng lấy từ đó. Observe không tự đọc biến env identity.
- Khai báo traits `ObservationSource` và `LegacyFrictionSource` cho các crate khác triển khai.

## 4. Current High-Level Components

This table is a compact navigation surface, not a full replacement for the advisory docs.

| Component | Current role | Current source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Work Lifecycle Engine / Work Driver | Domain-agnostic work-unit lifecycle, status board, claim/return, human gates. Does not own stage or sequencing (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), [workflow.md](workflow/spec.md)): execution and progress authority for a case on the ledger is the Workflow case, and Work keeps the status lifecycle, claim/return, slots, settlement and the `workflowRunId` pointer; the coding step FSM stays the authority for coding items until the coding cutover. Owns worker slots (`OccupancyPort`), and fail-safe claim settlement (`fgos return --to blocked`). | [../architect/component-boundary/component-boundary-advisory.md](../architect/component-boundary/component-boundary-advisory.md) |
| Workflow (guide + case; `src/workflow/**`) | Component Workflow with two entities, guide and case (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), partially supersedes 0048 §2 and 0049 §4; behaviour per [workflow.md](workflow/spec.md), implementation follows its plan). Human review gates. A consumer of Git's Land and Sync; owns no git mutation of its own. Single authority for the guide schema and its pinned snapshot per case; the case ledger (approved frame, reservations, route/deviation events, gate answers bound to subject digests, receipts, milestone projection, close); admission (is a proposed activity lawful now, against a closed catalog of machine checks); the worktree binding record (keyed by worktree root identity, with a generation) and the frame counters. Implements the AdmissionPort that Execution Core declares; imports flow Workflow → Execution Core only. Chooses no order: the agent proposes, the case admits and records; the Playbook proposer proposes through admission like any agent. Admission predicates, projection and the port implementation sit at infra or lower; the Playbook proposer at use-case. The ledger stays the JSONL under `advance`, hardened in place (fsync before release, reader fails closed); not an Event Store consumer in this cutover (owner 2026-10-19). Consumer of Execution Core and Git. Never owns who/model/persona, verify execution, locks, writer identity, merge or Work status. | [workflow/spec.md](workflow/spec.md), [runner/spec.md](runner/spec.md) |
| Execution Core (Unit, Unit run, `bind()`, Pattern cộng tác, cửa `fgos run`, posture) | Single authority for how a Unit runs (mechanism, posture, gates), through a single run door for new work (`fgos run` via `src/runner/execution/run.mjs`, herdr pane default, cli fallback), OS confinement posture for both herdr and cli, verifiable mutating gate. Strictly forbids L3 Work lifecycle dependencies (`src/state/**`). Owns the AdmissionPort interface (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), [workflow.md](workflow/spec.md)) (resolve the target worktree's binding, admit, settle), never the admission decision; every `runUnit` caller with writes (the run door, the Playbook proposer and the Work paths running today) injects Workflow's real implementation from the day it lands, and the port accepts an `advance` hold the caller already has. `runUnit` refuses a mutating Unit with no port, and a standalone write passes only on an affirmative `unbound`. The door resolves the caller's authority context conjunctively after pattern resolution and before `bind()`; the port stays present at the mutating gate, which re-checks subject-bound consent at effect; the door sets the case context in the worker's launch env and strips any inherited one. A nested writing dispatch from a confined worker is refused by name (owner 2026-10-19). It no longer chooses a seat: which executor, model, effort, tier and account an agent seat gets, and where it goes on failure, belongs to Seat Binding (next row, D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding)); `src/runner/execution/bind.mjs` is the thin facade that collects machine facts and asks it. Persona files are loaded by `agent-definitions` (names and paths by Convention). | [runner/spec.md](runner/spec.md) |
| Seat Binding (`fgos-seat-binding`) | Single authority for "which executor, invocation, model, effort, tier and account runs this agent seat, and where it goes on failure", with the reason for each part ([spec §3](seat-binding/spec.md)). Two pure stages in a Rust crate (static policy, then ranking) behind the internal route `fgos internal seat-binding bind\|ladder`; thin Node client `src/seat-binding/client.mjs` (fails closed; inside an activated release the activation host answers). Depends only on `fgos-host-runtime`. Agent seats only: a capability served by a tool executor keeps its own path. Account state (lease, release, quarantine, probe) is reached through the provider-capacity port: the facade reads the account view outside the provider lock, and the lease takes exactly the account the crate named; no host exec runs under that lock. Owns the tier ladder (the source of the config `$comment`). Does not own the seat list (the seat resolver, from pattern and workflow `seats:`), launching, transport, confinement, admission or persona loading. | [seat-binding/spec.md](seat-binding/spec.md), `packages/seat-binding/rust`, `src/seat-binding/client.mjs` |
| Collaboration Patterns (Execution Core) | Domain-neutral small collaboration loops (`solo`, `reviewed`, `panel`) and presets (`consult`, `research-fan-out`, `rfc`). Replaces retired coordination engine. | [runner/spec.md](runner/spec.md) |
| Herdr (Transport chính + Bề mặt quan sát) | Transport mặc định cho out-of-process runs, pane execution liveness, plugin `herdr-dashboard/` (TUI trong pane herdr + pick/pane supervisor; herdr nạp qua `herdr-plugin.toml`). | [herdr-web-dashboard/spec.md](herdr-web-dashboard/spec.md) |
| fgos Gateway | Tiến trình detached duy nhất phục vụ REST API (`/v1`, hợp đồng CTR010), MCP `search`/`execute` trên cùng cổng, và bundle web dashboard nhúng sẵn (`apps/fgos-gateway/`: `gateway.rs`, `mcp.rs`, `cf_access.rs`, `remote_invocation.rs`, `web/`). Vòng đời duy nhất qua `fgos gateway start\|status\|stop`; không phải một phần của herdr và không phải "herdr-gateway" (tên đó chỉ repo tham chiếu ngoài). Dùng chung với `herdr-dashboard` lớp adapter CLI fgos tại `packages/herdr-fgos-common/rust` (`fgos.rs`, `settings.rs`, trait `WorkItemSource`). | [herdr-web-dashboard/spec.md](herdr-web-dashboard/spec.md) |
| Dispatch Transport & Confinement | Machine backend registry, isolation confinement (`bwrap` v1 driver, attestation storage, fail-closed probes), executor adapters; the `bwrap` driver calls the credential renewal module at provisioning (`copyCredentialFiles`, the write-back marker) and removing a private home (`confinement/cleanup.mjs`) calls it again for write-back (dependency confinement → provider capacity, for the account lock only). | [agent-confinement/spec.md](agent-confinement/spec.md) |
| Run Result Evaluator | Evidence/confidence boundary for assignment run results. | [../architect/agent-coordination/architecture/evidence-and-results.md](../architect/agent-coordination/architecture/evidence-and-results.md) |
| Domain Components And Extension Layer | Domain-specific behavior, workflows, skills, task specs, doctrine. L2 prose no longer picks executors or mechanisms (lớp matching L2 cũ đã thu hồi per 0048); thin driver `fgos-run` delegates directly to the Workflow door (`fgos workflow start`) and P1 Execution Core (`fgos run`); a conductor names the Workflow case on each dispatch. | [../../domains/](../../domains/), [../architect/domainization/](../architect/domainization/) |
| Host And Surface Layer | CLI, fgos Gateway (REST/MCP/web), `herdr-dashboard` plugin and other Herdr surfaces into platform engines. | Host invocation and gateway docs |
| Packaging-Distribution | Runtime packaging, install, activation, setup/doctor readiness. | [packaging-distribution/README.md](packaging-distribution/README.md) |
| Knowledge, Learning, And Documentation Registry | Retrospective learning, doc registry, end-user docs index, trace/evolve signals. | Knowledge and docs registry docs |
| Observe (Metrics & Friction) | Measurement and friction tracking across substrate entities (cases, runs, sessions, friction, snapshots). Owned in Rust (`packages/observe/rust`), native routing. | [observe/spec.md](observe/spec.md) |
| Convention (Executable Names & Placement) | Platform-core authority for deterministic artifact names, repository-relative placement, path classification, and conformance checking. Implemented; owns no state and depends only on `fgos-host-runtime`. | [convention/spec.md](convention/spec.md) |
| Identity (foundation; today the local session writer id) | Foundation authority for identities, today for "who is the writer of this process" (`{id, source}`). One implementation, the Rust crate `fgos-identity` (`packages/identity/rust`, native verb `fgos identity`); Observe calls it in process, Node through the facade `src/util/session-identity.mjs` over the combined addon's `sessionIdentity` namespace. Also mints the writer id of an attempt (`att-<attemptId>`) and carries the launcher's env scrub the gate applies. Also mints and reads the machine id (`<stateRoot>/machine-id`, optional `machine-alias`; `fgos identity machine`, doctor row `identity-machine-id`) and derives the machine handle; also reads and, on an explicit `fgos identity project --init`, mints the project id (the tracked file `.fgos/project.json`; doctor row `identity-project-id`; the provider reads the Git component for the trusted main root and the remote default branch); the one validator of the id shape lives here. The host provider sits behind the default cargo feature `provider` (needs `fgos-host-runtime`, `fgos-holder-lock`, `fgos-convention`, `fgos-git`); Event Store and the node addon depend on the library with `default-features = false`, so the event log never pulls the host runtime. The process-tree adapter reads `/proc` through `fgos-process` (a plain dependency, an L0 leaf, not behind `provider`). Observe depends on it; the run supervisor's controller half calls the mint and, through the library without `provider`, the ISO-8601 UTC clock `text::iso_utc_now` (host-runtime's `civil_time` stays the clock of the crates that already sit on the host runtime; it cannot call identity, whose provider depends on it). The machine-id mint reaches Node through the addon's `sessionIdentity.mintMachineId`, wrapped by `src/util/identity-mint.mjs`. Grants no lock or claim authority. | [identity/spec.md](identity/spec.md) |
| Terminal-control (L2) | Foundation component for "which pane does this key run in" on a terminal multiplexer, usable without a run. Rust crate `fgos-terminal-control` (`packages/terminal-control/rust`) with a key-addressed upper port and a driver port with declared capabilities (herdr first; Windows declares none). Writes only the allocation record; closes only panes it allocated, never a tab; Node reaches it through the internal route `fgos internal terminal-control`, no user verb. Dependency one way: run supervisor → Terminal-control (the supervisor holds the key, the attempt id, never a pane). Node migration done; setup adds the `terminal` config section and `<stateRoot>/terminal`, doctor runs `terminal-control`, `terminal-config` and `terminal-allocations`. | [terminal-control/spec.md](terminal-control/spec.md) |
| Process Facts & Control (L0) | Single authority for "is this process tuple `{host, bootId, pidNs, pid, startTime}` alive, dead or unknown" (`judge`, one vector file run by cargo), for signalling a process by identity (`pidfd` on Linux, never a bare pid), for spawning with an explicit fd mapping, and for the domain primitives `domain_is_empty`/`domain_kill_all` the predecessor rule of holder-lock needs. Never spawns to read facts, never kills by bare pid, never reads mtime, knows no run, lock or pane. Rust crate `fgos-process` (`packages/process/rust`), one driver per OS; Node reaches it only through the in-process door (`src/native/door.mjs` → `src/runner/dispatch/process-identity.mjs`, six exports, at most 60 lines, no `/proc`, no `process.kill`); reconcile imports the thin client. Callers reclaim only on `dead` and count a process stopped only after a `sent` signal and a `dead` judgement; `unknown` always holds. Loader errors `process-door-unavailable` and `process-door-not-shipped` fail closed with a next step. No Node file judges a recorded process or signals a bare pid: the only `process.kill` calls left signal the process group of a child the same code just spawned, and the remaining `/proc` readers (lock-holder fd scan, doctor checks, confinement probes) are listed with their reasons in `test/process/one-door.test.mjs`, which fails on any other site. The doctor row kept is `process-containment`. The gate primitives (subreaper, PDEATHSIG, PID namespace, tty) stay with the run supervisor; the containment port lives in this crate (row below). Depends only on the OS. | [process/spec.md](process/spec.md) |
| Holder-lock (L1) | Single authority for "who holds which resource", as the kernel sees it: kernel locks on open file descriptions behind one OS-neutral port (`acquire`, `release`, `run_borrowed`, `probe`, `holders`, `guarantee`), the lock registry (`packages/holder-lock/contracts/lock-registry.v1.json`: every lock's kind, scope, rank and path), lock order inside one `LockScope`, the description rules, the predecessor-domain rule and the single state-root resolution. Never reads writer identity, never takes a lock from a live holder, never derives a decision from a pid, TTL or mtime. Rust crate `fgos-holder-lock` (`packages/holder-lock/rust`) plus the `holderLock` namespace of the combined addon, which the facade takes once through a one-shot capability (Node runs every lock operation in process on Linux and macOS), and the four surviving internal routes `fgos internal lock-fd` (borrowed check and shared try, for the git hook), `lock-hold` (Windows), `quiesce-scan` and `lock-borrow-vectors`; Node only through the facade `src/holder-lock/`, which never exposes an fd. The state root is the host's pin, else the door's `holderLock.stateRoot`; the checkout channel `node bin/fgos.mjs` is unsupported for lock verbs. Depends on Process Facts & Control and the kernel. Owns the cold locks (gateway, runner, sessions, advance, reconcile, recovery, full-suite, provider account/state, dispatch cwd) and the main checkout mutex (one door `withMainCheckout`, git children and the pre-commit hook borrow the lock through the description, no pid or TTL), the merge slot and `worktree-admin`; `fgos lock fence` is the one door for a hung live holder. `advance` follows Shape C (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), owner 2026-10-19, [workflow.md](workflow/spec.md)): a conductor case holds it for one reserve or one release/settle; the Playbook proposer holds it for the life of its loop, so its holder is the proposer's liveness, as today; a dispatch naming a live playbook case from inside its own Unit is refused by name. `answer` never appends directly: it writes the gate-answer file and tries `advance` once. The worktree binding is one exclusively created file per worktree, not a registry row. No new lock row; rank stays 80; no re-rank for an Event Store cutover. It does not own the state store's hot mutex (`state`, `porting-events`: `withStateTx` in `src/state/hot-lock.mjs`, which replaced `events.lock`, `claims.lock` and `porting/events.lock`): the state store owns that mechanism, a temporary one until the store moves to Rust, and takes only its cleanup lock from this component. The main door's `.fgos` checkpoint is a detachable adapter, so the lock core knows nothing of the event log. | [holder-lock/spec.md](holder-lock/spec.md) |
| Containment port (L0) | Single authority for "which processes belong to this attempt, and are there any left": an OS-neutral process domain per attempt (`create`, `spawn_in`, `is_empty`, `kill_all`, `guarantee`) with one driver per OS (`bwrap-pidns` and `linux-pgroup` on Linux, `windows-job`, `macos-tree`), each reporting a guarantee level (`kernel` or `best-effort`) and its named escapes. Knows no attempt beyond the id that names a domain, and no envelope, lock or pane. Module `containment` of the Rust crate `fgos-process` (`packages/process/rust`), contract `packages/process/contracts/containment.port.v1.json`; depends only on the OS. The `linux-pgroup` driver sets no subreaper on its caller and answers `is_empty` `unknown`, never `empty`, when a seen or listed member cannot be judged or read. Node has no caller of `create`, `spawn_in`, `guarantee` or the domain calls, so the addon exports none of them. | [process/spec.md](process/spec.md#10-containment-port) |
| Durable file (L0 leaf) | Single authority for how an fgOS record reaches disk when its loss must not go unnoticed: temp file, fsync of the file, install (replace, or create-only without replacing), fsync of the directory; every error says the step it failed at and which effect already happened (`installed: created \| already-exists \| none`); the file mode is explicit, and an omitted or invalid mode is refused by name (`durable-file-mode-invalid`) before anything is written. A create-only writer that finds the name already there leaves without a directory fsync. Rust crate `fgos-durable-file` (`packages/durable-file/rust`); Node through the door exports `replaceDurably` and `installOnce` in `src/native/door.mjs`, which remove the retained temporary on failure. Node keeps its per-module no-fsync helpers (no shared write helper), each naming its temporary with `uniqueTmpTag()`; the mode-preserving trust store, copy-then-rename and Work-owned writes stay. Accepted duplication: the private temp-then-rename helpers of the run supervisor (`supervise.rs`, `adopt.rs`, `supervise/windows.rs`) and holder-lock (`route/hold.rs`, `predecessor.rs`) do not fsync, because a heartbeat fsync on every tick would add I/O to every live run. Node budget: the Node replace and create-only helpers that already fsynced are deleted (target Node −110). Depends only on the OS. | This row, until a spec of its own exists |
| Canonical JSON (L0 leaf) | Single authority for the bytes of canonical JSON: RFC 8785 member order by UTF-16 code units and ECMAScript number text; input that is not JSON is refused by name. Rust crate `fgos-canonical-json` (`packages/canonical-json/rust`, `canonical_json`, `canonical_line`), vectors in `packages/canonical-json/contracts/vectors/`; Node through the door export `canonicalJson(value)` (`src/native/door.mjs`), which serialises with `JSON.stringify` (so a `Date` becomes its `toJSON` text) and hands the text to Rust, and refuses a hole, a non-finite number or a value `JSON.stringify` cannot serialise with `canonical-json-not-json` and drops an `undefined` member as `JSON.stringify` does. Node budget: one re-export line. Accepted exceptions, each with its reason: `recovery-planner.mjs` keeps its own `stableStringify` (its module contract is purity, its import set is pinned to `node:crypto`, and its stored records hold only hash outputs); `effective-execution-contract.mjs` and the release-manifest producer and verifier pair stay together until the Packaging plan moves them as one; `trust-store.mjs` `sortedJson` stays because it must match codex's own byte order, not RFC 8785. Depends only on `serde_json` and `ryu-js`. | This row, until a spec of its own exists |
| YAML Document (L0 leaf; spec signed 2026-10-22; Rust crate and Rust consumers done, Node door not started) | Single authority for reading, editing and merging YAML text: a lossless document with semantic value and positions, two parse profiles (`strict-config` for config files, `tool` for workflows, personas, units and manifests, the latter keeping today's js-yaml door contract), edits that keep every untouched byte, comment blocks as positioned text with an injection guard, and a merge primitive whose per-path rules the caller supplies. Knows no config key, file scope, default, lock or comment grammar. Rust crate `fgos-yaml-doc` (planned `packages/yaml-doc/rust`); Node through the native door namespace `yaml` behind the kept facade `src/util/yaml.mjs`; replaces the vendored js-yaml (RUL101 superseded when it lands); `frontmatter.mjs` and `distill.mjs` stay on their own paths. Depends only on its parser crate. | [yaml-document/spec.md](yaml-document/spec.md) |
| Config (L1; spec signed 2026-10-22; Rust crate, section schemas and standard done, not yet wired to any caller) | Single authority for fgOS configuration: which files are config (project `.fgos/config.yaml` over global `~/.fgos/config.yaml` over the read-only standard shipped with the release; config files hold only differences; account pools and the gateway token under `~/.fgos/private/`, hidden from confined workers), the schema dialect and engine (descriptors are data shipped by each section's owner under `core/config-schema/`), the effective snapshot with provenance, the three write doors (`init`, `doctor --fix`, `fgos config`) and their one-file transaction (new locks `project-config` and `global-config`, compare-and-swap on byte revision, Durable File replace), the `@fgos:doc` / `@fgos:why` comment grammar and when a reason is required, the config doctor checks and JSON-to-YAML migration. Reads never write. Never owns YAML syntax (YAML Document), lock mechanism (Holder-lock), secret values (Secrets), section meaning or cross-field rules (each section owner), or bootstrap JSON files. Rust crate `fgos-config` (planned `packages/config/rust`); Node through the native door namespace `config`, replacing `src/config/` and every direct reader. Depends on YAML Document, Holder-lock, Durable File and Secrets; acquires its own locks without reading config. | [config/spec.md](config/spec.md) |
| Git (foundation) | Single authority for repository facts, typed Git operations and their recovery WAL: every fgOS mutation of local objects, refs, index, worktrees and worktree registration, the local side of fetch and push, and operation recovery, through typed ports (Inspect, Refs, Worktree, ScopedCommit, Sync, Land, SafeRestore, RepositoryConfig, Remote, Recovery, Publication); no public `git(args)` port. Owns no business approval, Work lifecycle, event semantics or lock mechanism. Consumers: Workflow, Execution Core, Work, Event Store, setup. Depends on Holder-lock, Process Facts & Control and Session Identity; imports no consumer. Rust crate `fgos-git` (`packages/git/rust`); Node reaches it only through the one combined N-API addon (`packages/git/node-addon`) that also links `fgos-event-store`, via the facade `src/git/`. Implemented through Git phase 07 (callers moved onto the typed ports); the whole-product one-door gate (`git-mutation-one-door`, spec §12) and the phase 08 proofs land with the Git plan's final release. | [git/spec.md](git/spec.md) |
| Event Store (foundation) | Single authority for how an fgOS event becomes durable, is sealed into git objects on per-machine `refs/fgos/*`, is shared across machines and is read back: the v4 envelope and stream registry, the per-stream open logs and their `event-append`/`event-seal` locks, seal and recovery, the reader with coverage, causal order and cursor, sync, and the store side of the `fgos events` verbs (`src/verbs/events/`). Planned consumers: Work, porting, observe, decisions; each owns its types, gate, reducer and view, and the store imports none of them (`packages/event-store/contracts/consumers.v1.json` is the only registry). Depends on Git's Publication port (the only door to `refs/fgos/*`), Holder-lock and Session Identity. Rust crate `fgos-event-store` (`packages/event-store/rust`); Node only through the facade `src/event-store/` over the one combined N-API addon shared with `fgos-git`. Dormant on main: store layer proven (2026-10-20), no consumer registered; the Work cutover is the WORK lane. | [event-store/spec.md](event-store/spec.md) |
| Run Supervisor (L4) | One Rust process per attempt that owns the attempt after the controller handed it over: holds the attempt lock and the cwd lease, creates the containment domain, starts the launch gate, watches the soft deadline and idle, publishes the receipt and the per-step receipts, runs the post-receipt steps and owns the adopt door (`fgos internal adopt`, one door for resume, recover, scan and home cleanup). A supervisor that dies leaves the agent running; adopt settles it. Never knows a pane or a terminal, never picks a provider or retries, never judges the work (Run Result Evaluator inside the Node `settle-attempt` step). Crate `fgos-run-supervisor` (`packages/run-supervisor/rust`), routes `fgos internal supervise\|gate\|adopt\|attempt-step` (protocol 1, not in help), Node client and steps in `src/run-supervisor/`. Depends on Containment port, Process Facts & Control, Holder-lock and agent-protocol. Two launch modes: `direct` (headless process) and `terminal` (an agent in a terminal-control pane, addressed by the attempt id; the supervisor listens on an attempt socket, drives the pane through the agent protocol and ends with a `release-slot` step). Depends also on Terminal-control (in process, by key). | [run-supervisor/spec.md](run-supervisor/spec.md) |
| Launch gate (L4, part of the run supervisor) | The process root of the agent inside the containment domain (pid 1 of a fresh PID namespace on Linux): owns the agent's IO (capture files, stdin; in `terminal` mode the pane's tty, with the agent as foreground group), refuses to run the agent without GO (in `terminal` mode GO arrives over the attempt socket with the attempt lock and cwd lease as `SCM_RIGHTS`, the peer uid is checked, and the gate runs in the pane, so the gate holds the attempt lock and outlives a dead supervisor), applies the environment scrub and the attempt writer id, reaps every orphan with `waitpid(-1)` for the whole attempt, enforces the hard ceiling (SIGTERM, `dispatch.gateKillGraceMs`, SIGKILL) on its own clock and publishes `gate-exit.json` once the domain is empty. `fgos internal gate`; same crate and spec as the supervisor. | [run-supervisor/spec.md](run-supervisor/spec.md#5-supervisor-and-gate) |
| Agent protocol (L3) | Pure per-CLI adapters (claude, codex, agy, pi, omp) that read what an agent CLI showed (capture tail, exit, outbox) and name the result (`completed`, `blocked(login\|trust-dialog\|usage-limit)`, `needs-human`, `exited`); decide stdin policy and the activity source for idle. Never builds argv (that stays with the executor configuration through `resolveExecutorCommand`), never retries, no dependency on terminal-control, locks or attempts. Direct and terminal adapters; the terminal ones read the pane through `AgentIo` (`screen`, `inspect`) wired by the supervisor to terminal-control. Crate `fgos-agent-protocol` (`packages/agent-protocol/rust`). | [agent-protocol/spec.md](agent-protocol/spec.md) |
| Agent Mailbox (L4, signed at G0 on 2026-10-20; implementation not started) | Single authority for "how a message from one agent session is placed into the context of the right live head of a CLI on this machine, with an honest delivery report, and never as the user's input": the envelope, the delivery state machine (`recorded`, `in-flight`, `offered`, `refused`), the registry of heads (name, per-process generation, process `Record`), the channel-protection policies, the peer frame, and the per-CLI hook payload shape and non-terminal wake channels (the Claude Code scoped socket, `codex queue`). Recipients are independently started interactive heads, never a runner Unit attempt, a subagent or a teammate. Owns one runtime-state record per project at the main checkout's `.fgos` (not event truth, never replayed, never pushed). First slice imports only `fgos-process`, `fgos-holder-lock`, `fgos-durable-file` and `fgos-identity`; its core crate `fgos-mailbox-core` depends on serde alone. Never owns writer identity (Session Identity), process liveness (Process Facts & Control), the main-checkout `.fgos` resolver (the host), pane access (Terminal-control), typing or screen reading (Agent protocol; a later part), hook installation (the setup installer), locks (Holder-lock), communication authorization or case budgets (coordination foundation), or steering a Unit attempt (the runner). Rust crates `fgos-mailbox-core` and `fgos-mailbox` (planned: `packages/mailbox/rust`). | [agent-mailbox/spec.md](agent-mailbox/spec.md) |

## 4. Current High-Level Components

This table is a compact navigation surface, not a full replacement for the advisory docs.

| Component | Current role | Current source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Work Lifecycle Engine / Work Driver | Domain-agnostic work-unit lifecycle, status board, claim/return, human gates. Does not own stage or sequencing (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), [workflow.md](workflow/spec.md)): execution and progress authority for a case on the ledger is the Workflow case, and Work keeps the status lifecycle, claim/return, slots, settlement and the `workflowRunId` pointer; the coding step FSM stays the authority for coding items until the coding cutover. Owns worker slots (`OccupancyPort`), and fail-safe claim settlement (`fgos return --to blocked`). | [../architect/component-boundary/component-boundary-advisory.md](../architect/component-boundary/component-boundary-advisory.md) |
| Workflow (guide + case; `src/workflow/**`) | Component Workflow with two entities, guide and case (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), partially supersedes 0048 §2 and 0049 §4; behaviour per [workflow.md](workflow/spec.md), implementation follows its plan). Human review gates. A consumer of Git's Land and Sync; owns no git mutation of its own. Single authority for the guide schema and its pinned snapshot per case; the case ledger (approved frame, reservations, route/deviation events, gate answers bound to subject digests, receipts, milestone projection, close); admission (is a proposed activity lawful now, against a closed catalog of machine checks); the worktree binding record (keyed by worktree root identity, with a generation) and the frame counters. Implements the AdmissionPort that Execution Core declares; imports flow Workflow → Execution Core only. Chooses no order: the agent proposes, the case admits and records; the Playbook proposer proposes through admission like any agent. Admission predicates, projection and the port implementation sit at infra or lower; the Playbook proposer at use-case. The ledger stays the JSONL under `advance`, hardened in place (fsync before release, reader fails closed); not an Event Store consumer in this cutover (owner 2026-10-19). Consumer of Execution Core and Git. Never owns who/model/persona, verify execution, locks, writer identity, merge or Work status. | [workflow/spec.md](workflow/spec.md), [runner/spec.md](runner/spec.md) |
| Execution Core (Unit, Unit run, `bind()`, Pattern cộng tác, cửa `fgos run`, posture) | Single authority for how a Unit runs (mechanism, posture, gates), through a single run door for new work (`fgos run` via `src/runner/execution/run.mjs`, herdr pane default, cli fallback), OS confinement posture for both herdr and cli, verifiable mutating gate. Strictly forbids L3 Work lifecycle dependencies (`src/state/**`). Owns the AdmissionPort interface (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), [workflow.md](workflow/spec.md)) (resolve the target worktree's binding, admit, settle), never the admission decision; every `runUnit` caller with writes (the run door, the Playbook proposer and the Work paths running today) injects Workflow's real implementation from the day it lands, and the port accepts an `advance` hold the caller already has. `runUnit` refuses a mutating Unit with no port, and a standalone write passes only on an affirmative `unbound`. The door resolves the caller's authority context conjunctively after pattern resolution and before `bind()`; the port stays present at the mutating gate, which re-checks subject-bound consent at effect; the door sets the case context in the worker's launch env and strips any inherited one. A nested writing dispatch from a confined worker is refused by name (owner 2026-10-19). It no longer chooses a seat: which executor, model, effort, tier and account an agent seat gets, and where it goes on failure, belongs to Seat Binding (next row, D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding)); `src/runner/execution/bind.mjs` is the thin facade that collects machine facts and asks it. Persona files are loaded by `agent-definitions` (names and paths by Convention). | [runner/spec.md](runner/spec.md) |
| Seat Binding (`fgos-seat-binding`) | Single authority for "which executor, invocation, model, effort, tier and account runs this agent seat, and where it goes on failure", with the reason for each part ([spec §3](seat-binding/spec.md)). Two pure stages in a Rust crate (static policy, then ranking) behind the internal route `fgos internal seat-binding bind\|ladder`; thin Node client `src/seat-binding/client.mjs` (fails closed; inside an activated release the activation host answers). Depends only on `fgos-host-runtime`. Agent seats only: a capability served by a tool executor keeps its own path. Account state (lease, release, quarantine, probe) is reached through the provider-capacity port: the facade reads the account view outside the provider lock, and the lease takes exactly the account the crate named; no host exec runs under that lock. Owns the tier ladder (the source of the config `$comment`). Does not own the seat list (the seat resolver, from pattern and workflow `seats:`), launching, transport, confinement, admission or persona loading. | [seat-binding/spec.md](seat-binding/spec.md), `packages/seat-binding/rust`, `src/seat-binding/client.mjs` |
| Collaboration Patterns (Execution Core) | Domain-neutral small collaboration loops (`solo`, `reviewed`, `panel`) and presets (`consult`, `research-fan-out`, `rfc`). Replaces retired coordination engine. | [runner/spec.md](runner/spec.md) |
| Herdr (Transport chính + Bề mặt quan sát) | Transport mặc định cho out-of-process runs, pane execution liveness, plugin `herdr-dashboard/` (TUI trong pane herdr + pick/pane supervisor; herdr nạp qua `herdr-plugin.toml`). | [herdr-web-dashboard/spec.md](herdr-web-dashboard/spec.md) |
| fgos Gateway | Tiến trình detached duy nhất phục vụ REST API (`/v1`, hợp đồng CTR010), MCP `search`/`execute` trên cùng cổng, và bundle web dashboard nhúng sẵn (`apps/fgos-gateway/`: `gateway.rs`, `mcp.rs`, `cf_access.rs`, `remote_invocation.rs`, `web/`). Never reads writer identity, never takes a lock from a live holder, never derives a decision from a pid, TTL or mtime. Rust crate `fgos-holder-lock` (`packages/holder-lock/rust`) plus the `holderLock` namespace of the combined addon, which the facade takes once through a one-shot capability (Node runs every lock operation in process on Linux and macOS), and the four surviving internal routes `fgos internal lock-fd` (borrowed check and shared try, for the git hook), `lock-hold` (Windows), `quiesce-scan` and `lock-borrow-vectors`; Node only through the facade `src/holder-lock/`, which never exposes an fd. The state root is the host's pin, else the door's `holderLock.stateRoot`; the checkout channel `node bin/fgos.mjs` is unsupported for lock verbs. Depends on Process Facts & Control and the kernel. Owns the cold locks (gateway, runner, sessions, advance, reconcile, recovery, full-suite, provider account/state, dispatch cwd) and the main checkout mutex (one door `withMainCheckout`, git children and the pre-commit hook borrow the lock through the description, no pid or TTL), the merge slot and `worktree-admin`; `fgos lock fence` is the one door for a hung live holder. `advance` follows Shape C (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), owner 2026-10-19, [workflow.md](workflow/spec.md)): a conductor case holds it for one reserve or one release/settle; the Playbook proposer holds it for the life of its loop, so its holder is the proposer's liveness, as today; a dispatch naming a live playbook case from inside its own Unit is refused by name. `answer` never appends directly: it writes the gate-answer file and tries `advance` once. The worktree binding is one exclusively created file per worktree, not a registry row. No new lock row; rank stays 80; no re-rank for an Event Store cutover. It does not own the state store's hot mutex (`state`, `porting-events`: `withStateTx` in `src/state/hot-lock.mjs`, which replaced `events.lock`, `claims.lock` and `porting/events.lock`): the state store owns that mechanism, a temporary one until the store moves to Rust, and takes only its cleanup lock from this component. The main door's `.fgos` checkpoint is a detachable adapter, so the lock core knows nothing of the event log. | [holder-lock/spec.md](holder-lock/spec.md) |
| Containment port (L0) | Single authority for "which processes belong to this attempt, and are there any left": an OS-neutral process domain per attempt (`create`, `spawn_in`, `is_empty`, `kill_all`, `guarantee`) with one driver per OS (`bwrap-pidns` and `linux-pgroup` on Linux, `windows-job`, `macos-tree`), each reporting a guarantee level (`kernel` or `best-effort`) and its named escapes. Knows no attempt beyond the id that names a domain, and no envelope, lock or pane. Module `containment` of the Rust crate `fgos-process` (`packages/process/rust`), contract `packages/process/contracts/containment.port.v1.json`; depends only on the OS. The `linux-pgroup` driver sets no subreaper on its caller and answers `is_empty` `unknown`, never `empty`, when a seen or listed member cannot be judged or read. Node has no caller of `create`, `spawn_in`, `guarantee` or the domain calls, so the addon exports none of them. | [process/spec.md](process/spec.md#10-containment-port) |
| Durable file (L0 leaf) | Single authority for how an fgOS record reaches disk when its loss must not go unnoticed: temp file, fsync of the file, install (replace, or create-only without replacing), fsync of the directory; every error says the step it failed at and which effect already happened (`installed: created \| already-exists \| none`); the file mode is explicit, and an omitted or invalid mode is refused by name (`durable-file-mode-invalid`) before anything is written. A create-only writer that finds the name already there leaves without a directory fsync. Rust crate `fgos-durable-file` (`packages/durable-file/rust`); Node through the door exports `replaceDurably` and `installOnce` in `src/native/door.mjs`, which remove the retained temporary on failure. Node keeps its per-module no-fsync helpers (no shared write helper), each naming its temporary with `uniqueTmpTag()`; the mode-preserving trust store, copy-then-rename and Work-owned writes stay. Accepted duplication: the private temp-then-rename helpers of the run supervisor (`supervise.rs`, `adopt.rs`, `supervise/windows.rs`) and holder-lock (`route/hold.rs`, `predecessor.rs`) do not fsync, because a heartbeat fsync on every tick would add I/O to every live run. Node budget: the Node replace and create-only helpers that already fsynced are deleted (target Node −110). Depends only on the OS. | This row, until a spec of its own exists |
| Canonical JSON (L0 leaf) | Single authority for the bytes of canonical JSON: RFC 8785 member order by UTF-16 code units and ECMAScript number text; input that is not JSON is refused by name. Rust crate `fgos-canonical-json` (`packages/canonical-json/rust`, `canonical_json`, `canonical_line`), vectors in `packages/canonical-json/contracts/vectors/`; Node through the door export `canonicalJson(value)` (`src/native/door.mjs`), which serialises with `JSON.stringify` (so a `Date` becomes its `toJSON` text) and hands the text to Rust, and refuses a hole, a non-finite number or a value `JSON.stringify` cannot serialise with `canonical-json-not-json` and drops an `undefined` member as `JSON.stringify` does. Node budget: one re-export line. Accepted exceptions, each with its reason: `recovery-planner.mjs` keeps its own `stableStringify` (its module contract is purity, its import set is pinned to `node:crypto`, and its stored records hold only hash outputs); `effective-execution-contract.mjs` and the release-manifest producer and verifier pair stay together until the Packaging plan moves them as one; `trust-store.mjs` `sortedJson` stays because it must match codex's own byte order, not RFC 8785. Depends only on `serde_json` and `ryu-js`. | This row, until a spec of its own exists |
| YAML Document (L0 leaf; spec signed 2026-10-22; Rust crate, Rust consumers and the Node door done) | Single authority for reading, editing and merging YAML text: a lossless document with semantic value and positions, two parse profiles (`strict-config` for config files, `tool` for workflows, personas, units and manifests, the latter keeping today's js-yaml door contract), edits that keep every untouched byte, comment blocks as positioned text with an injection guard, and a merge primitive whose per-path rules the caller supplies. Knows no config key, file scope, default, lock or comment grammar. Rust crate `fgos-yaml-doc` (`packages/yaml-doc/rust`); Node through the native door namespace `yaml` behind the kept facade `src/util/yaml.mjs`; replaced the vendored js-yaml (RUL101 superseded by RUL108, 2026-10-23); `frontmatter.mjs` and `distill.mjs` stay on their own paths. Depends only on its parser crate. | [yaml-document/spec.md](yaml-document/spec.md) |
| Config (L1; spec signed 2026-10-22; Rust crate, section schemas and standard done, not yet wired to any caller) | Single authority for fgOS configuration: which files are config (project `.fgos/config.yaml` over global `~/.fgos/config.yaml` over the read-only standard shipped with the release; config files hold only differences; account pools and the gateway token under `~/.fgos/private/`, hidden from confined workers), the schema dialect and engine (descriptors are data shipped by each section's owner under `core/config-schema/`), the effective snapshot with provenance, the three write doors (`init`, `doctor --fix`, `fgos config`) and their one-file transaction (new locks `project-config` and `global-config`, compare-and-swap on byte revision, Durable File replace), the `@fgos:doc` / `@fgos:why` comment grammar and when a reason is required, the config doctor checks and JSON-to-YAML migration. Reads never write. Never owns YAML syntax (YAML Document), lock mechanism (Holder-lock), secret values (Secrets), section meaning or cross-field rules (each section owner), or bootstrap JSON files. Rust crate `fgos-config` (planned `packages/config/rust`); Node through the native door namespace `config`, replacing `src/config/` and every direct reader. Depends on YAML Document, Holder-lock, Durable File and Secrets; acquires its own locks without reading config. | [config/spec.md](config/spec.md) |
| Git (foundation) | Single authority for repository facts, typed Git operations and their recovery WAL: every fgOS mutation of local objects, refs, index, worktrees and worktree registration, the local side of fetch and push, and operation recovery, through typed ports (Inspect, Refs, Worktree, ScopedCommit, Sync, Land, SafeRestore, RepositoryConfig, Remote, Recovery, Publication); no public `git(args)` port. Its Publication port is the only door to `refs/fgos/*`, and Event Store is the only production writer of event refs through it. Owns no business approval, Work lifecycle, event semantics or lock mechanism. Consumers: Workflow, Execution Core, Work, Event Store, setup. Depends on Holder-lock, Process Facts & Control and Session Identity; imports no consumer. Rust crate `fgos-git` (`packages/git/rust`); Node reaches it only through the one combined N-API addon (`packages/git/node-addon`) that also links `fgos-event-store`, via the facade `src/git/`. Implemented through Git phase 07 (callers moved onto the typed ports); the whole-product one-door gate (`git-mutation-one-door`, spec §12) and the phase 08 proofs land with the Git plan's final release. | [git/spec.md](git/spec.md) |
| Event Store (foundation) | Single authority for how an fgOS event becomes durable, is sealed into git objects on per-machine `refs/fgos/*`, is shared across machines and is read back: the v4 envelope and stream registry, the per-stream open logs and their `event-append`/`event-seal` locks, seal and recovery, the reader with coverage, causal order and cursor, sync, and the store side of the `fgos events` verbs (`src/verbs/events/`). Planned consumers: Work, porting, observe, decisions; each owns its types, gate, reducer and view, and the store imports none of them (`packages/event-store/contracts/consumers.v1.json` is the only registry). Depends on Git's Publication port (the only door to `refs/fgos/*`), Holder-lock and Session Identity. Rust crate `fgos-event-store` (`packages/event-store/rust`); Node only through the facade `src/event-store/` over the one combined N-API addon shared with `fgos-git`. Dormant on main: store layer proven (2026-10-20), no consumer registered; the Work cutover is the WORK lane. | [event-store/spec.md](event-store/spec.md) |
| Run Supervisor (L4) | One Rust process per attempt that owns the attempt after the controller handed it over: holds the attempt lock and the cwd lease, creates the containment domain, starts the launch gate, watches the soft deadline and idle, publishes the receipt and the per-step receipts, runs the post-receipt steps and owns the adopt door (`fgos internal adopt`, one door for resume, recover, scan and home cleanup). A supervisor that dies leaves the agent running; adopt settles it. Never knows a pane or a terminal, never picks a provider or retries, never judges the work (Run Result Evaluator inside the Node `settle-attempt` step). Crate `fgos-run-supervisor` (`packages/run-supervisor/rust`), routes `fgos internal supervise\|gate\|adopt\|attempt-step` (protocol 1, not in help), Node client and steps in `src/run-supervisor/`. Depends on Containment port, Process Facts & Control, Holder-lock and agent-protocol. Two launch modes: `direct` (headless process) and `terminal` (an agent in a terminal-control pane, addressed by the attempt id; the supervisor listens on an attempt socket, drives the pane through the agent protocol and ends with a `release-slot` step). Depends also on Terminal-control (in process, by key). | [run-supervisor/spec.md](run-supervisor/spec.md) |
| Launch gate (L4, part of the run supervisor) | The process root of the agent inside the containment domain (pid 1 of a fresh PID namespace on Linux): owns the agent's IO (capture files, stdin; in `terminal` mode the pane's tty, with the agent as foreground group), refuses to run the agent without GO (in `terminal` mode GO arrives over the attempt socket with the attempt lock and cwd lease as `SCM_RIGHTS`, the peer uid is checked, and the gate runs in the pane, so the gate holds the attempt lock and outlives a dead supervisor), applies the environment scrub and the attempt writer id, reaps every orphan with `waitpid(-1)` for the whole attempt, enforces the hard ceiling (SIGTERM, `dispatch.gateKillGraceMs`, SIGKILL) on its own clock and publishes `gate-exit.json` once the domain is empty. `fgos internal gate`; same crate and spec as the supervisor. | [run-supervisor/spec.md](run-supervisor/spec.md#5-supervisor-and-gate) |
| Agent protocol (L3) | Pure per-CLI adapters (claude, codex, agy, pi, omp) that read what an agent CLI showed (capture tail, exit, outbox) and name the result (`completed`, `blocked(login\|trust-dialog\|usage-limit)`, `needs-human`, `exited`); decide stdin policy and the activity source for idle. Never builds argv (that stays with the executor configuration through `resolveExecutorCommand`), never retries, no dependency on terminal-control, locks or attempts. Direct and terminal adapters; the terminal ones read the pane through `AgentIo` (`screen`, `inspect`) wired by the supervisor to terminal-control. Crate `fgos-agent-protocol` (`packages/agent-protocol/rust`). | [agent-protocol/spec.md](agent-protocol/spec.md) |
| Agent Mailbox (L4, signed at G0 on 2026-10-20; implementation not started) | Single authority for "how a message from one agent session is placed into the context of the right live head of a CLI on this machine, with an honest delivery report, and never as the user's input": the envelope, the delivery state machine (`recorded`, `in-flight`, `offered`, `refused`), the registry of heads (name, per-process generation, process `Record`), the channel-protection policies, the peer frame, and the per-CLI hook payload shape and non-terminal wake channels (the Claude Code scoped socket, `codex queue`). Recipients are independently started interactive heads, never a runner Unit attempt, a subagent or a teammate. Owns one runtime-state record per project at the main checkout's `.fgos` (not event truth, never replayed, never pushed). First slice imports only `fgos-process`, `fgos-holder-lock`, `fgos-durable-file` and `fgos-identity`; its core crate `fgos-mailbox-core` depends on serde alone. Never owns writer identity (Session Identity), process liveness (Process Facts & Control), the main-checkout `.fgos` resolver (the host), pane access (Terminal-control), typing or screen reading (Agent protocol; a later part), hook installation (the setup installer), locks (Holder-lock), communication authorization or case budgets (coordination foundation), or steering a Unit attempt (the runner). Rust crates `fgos-mailbox-core` and `fgos-mailbox` (planned: `packages/mailbox/rust`). | [agent-mailbox/spec.md](agent-mailbox/spec.md) |

Never owns writer identity (Session Identity), process liveness (Process Facts & Control), the main-checkout `.fgos` resolver (the host), pane access (Terminal-control), typing or screen reading (Agent protocol; a later part), hook installation (the setup installer), locks (Holder-lock), communication authorization or case budgets (coordination foundation), or steering a Unit attempt (the runner). Rust crates `fgos-mailbox-core` and `fgos-mailbox` (planned: `packages/mailbox/rust`). | [agent-mailbox/spec.md](agent-mailbox/spec.md) |
